legion.title: Same Deadline, Two Papers
text: {advisor} is submitting their own paper to the same deadline as {project}. "Could you run a few experiments on mine too? You're so fast."

choices.label: Help with both papers
choices.text: Both papers get submitted, and you sleep through most of the following weekend.

success.text: They rewrite your introduction in one evening, and it's much better.

failure.text: You run their experiments. Their notes on your intro arrive an hour after the deadline.

choices.label: Protect your own paper
choices.text: You say no, kindly, and give your own paper your full attention. {advisor} pulls an all-nighter and is a little cool all week.

legion.title: The Sign-Up Sheet
text: The lab shares one GPU, booked through a sheet taped to the server room door. Your three-day run for {project} would take every slot until Thursday.

choices.label: Book the whole week
choices.text: Your run finishes. Next to your name on the sheet, someone has drawn a very small frowning face.

choices.label: Take the night slots nobody wants
choices.text: Midnight to 6 am, five nights running. The run finishes, and you learn every sound the server makes.

success.text: With a smaller model and a smarter sample, it runs in one afternoon and still answers your question.

failure.text: The small run tells you nothing, so you add your name to the bottom of the sheet.

legion.title: The Warmest Letter
text: {advisor} sends you a copy of the recommendation letter they wrote for you. It's two pages long and specific about everything. You read it twice.

choices.label: Thank them in person
choices.text: They wave it off: "I only wrote down what's true." You both pretend not to be moved.

choices.label: Use it for three more applications
choices.text: You spend a long evening on three sets of forms. Each one goes out with a great letter behind it.

choices.label: Save it for the hard weeks
choices.text: You put it in a folder called "read this". You'll open it more often than you expect.

legion.title: How Does This Fit Aim 2?
text: Your meeting opens the way every meeting opens: "Before we start, how does this fit Aim 2?" Today, honestly, {project} doesn't.

choices.label: Reframe {project} around Aim 2
choices.text: Two slides later, your project fits Aim 2 perfectly. It is also slightly less interesting.

choices.label: Pitch it as a future Aim 4

success.text: "Aim 4. For the renewal. I like it." Your project is now in next year's grant.

failure.text: There is no Aim 4. There are three aims, and by the end of the meeting you know all of them by heart.

choices.label: Keep going and hope it passes
choices.text: It doesn't pass. The same question opens next week's meeting, and the one after that.

legion.title: Renewal Week
text: Grant renewal week. The whole lab pauses research to write progress summaries. The shared document is 61 pages long and has a table of contents for its table of contents.

choices.label: Write your summary carefully
choices.text: You write two pages on your year. On paper, it was a better year than it felt.

choices.label: Volunteer to edit the whole thing
choices.text: Sixty-one pages become forty. {advisor} calls it the cleanest renewal in years, and remembers who did it.

success.text: You write one tight page before lunch and are back to research by 1 pm.

failure.text: It comes back with one note: "More on Aim 2, please." The hour becomes two days.

legion.title: "thoughts?"
text: Over the weekend, {advisor} sends you 14 papers, one email each. Every subject line says "thoughts?". Your meeting is Monday at 10.

choices.label: Read all 14 by Monday
choices.text: You arrive with notes on every paper. {advisor} has moved on to a 15th, but is clearly impressed.

success.text: It's one idea in 14 disguises. You name it in one sentence, and {advisor} lights up.

failure.text: You find a common thread. It isn't the one they meant.

choices.label: Read two properly, ask about the rest
choices.text: "Oh, those were just for fun." Luckily, your two were the important ones.

legion.title: Best Paper, Other Lab
text: A best paper award goes to another lab, for the idea {advisor} emailed you at 2 am eight months ago. You still have the email. It was three lines long.

choices.label: Forward the email to {advisor}
choices.text: "Ha! Told you." They're delighted, and their next idea arrives at 2 am.

success.text: You spot the follow-up the winners missed. Your short paper is online within two weeks, and people read it.

failure.text: Eleven other labs had the same follow-up idea that week.

choices.label: Start a folder for 2 am ideas
choices.text: Every late-night idea now gets a real read the next morning. Most are wild, but one might not be.

legion.title: Unlimited Compute, Limited Lawyers
text: Thanks to {advisor}'s company, your compute for {project} was unlimited. Now every result needs legal review before you can submit. Legal estimates six to eight weeks.

choices.label: Submit it for review and wait
choices.text: Legal approves, with one change: "outperforms" becomes "compares favorably to", everywhere.

success.text: {advisor} sends one email to the right person. Approval arrives in three days.

failure.text: They try. Legal now has two questions instead of one.

choices.label: Rerun the key results on campus
choices.text: The university cluster is slow, but its results need no lawyer. Your paper is a little smaller now.

legion.title: A Product Manager Joins
text: {advisor} brings a product manager from the company to your research meeting. Ten minutes in, they ask about the roadmap for {project}, and its "go-to-market".

success.text: They love it and ask for a demo next month. You've never had a customer before.

failure.text: They ask about daily active users. You have twelve participants and a consent form.

choices.label: Ask what their users struggle with
choices.text: They talk for 40 minutes. It's the best user research you've done all year, and the meeting runs long.

choices.label: Steer back to the research
choices.text: The product manager checks their phone. Your meeting stays a research meeting, and {advisor} looks a little disappointed.

legion.title: Already Arranged
text: You've barely sent out your internship applications when {advisor} mentions, between meetings, that they've "already talked to the team" at {company}. "You'll probably start in May."

choices.label: Thank them and stop worrying
choices.text: You cancel two interviews and relax. {advisor} seems pleased that you trust them.

choices.label: Keep your other options going
choices.text: You keep interviewing anyway, which is more work but keeps your options open.

choices.label: Ask for the research team instead

success.text: "Good call." One more email, and you're on the research team.

failure.text: "Research is full this year. The product team is great, though."

legion.title: Old Classmates
text: Your committee meeting opens with {advisor} and {committee} remembering grad school together, decades ago. Two more committee members were there too. Your slides wait patiently.

choices.label: Let the stories run
choices.text: Forty minutes of stories leave five minutes for questions, all of them easy. Everyone leaves in a great mood.

choices.label: Ask them to settle an old debate

success.text: The old debate turns out to be about your topic. They argue happily, and your thesis comes out sharper.

failure.text: They argue happily for the full hour. Your slides go unshown.

choices.label: Steer them to your slides
choices.text: You get real, tough feedback. {advisor} looks mildly sorry to miss the end of the story.

legion.title: Back, With a Term Sheet
text: {advisor} has been unreachable for two weeks. Today they walk into lab meeting, tanned, holding a term sheet. "Big news! Also, how's everyone's research?"

choices.label: Ask about the startup
choices.text: They talk about funding rounds for forty minutes. You follow about a third of it, and it's a fascinating third.

choices.label: Ask for two weeks of feedback, now

success.text: They read everything you sent while they were gone, in one sitting. The feedback is excellent.

failure.text: "Can you resend those? My inbox is a disaster." You resend all six.

choices.label: Report the calls you made alone
choices.text: You made three decisions while they were gone. {advisor} approves two and reverses the third without comment.

legion.title: The CTO Down the Hall
text: A launch announcement reveals that {labmate} is the CTO of {advisor}'s newest startup. That explains the second laptop, and all the 4 pm "dentist appointments".

choices.label: Ask {labmate} how it all works
choices.text: Over coffee they explain how equity works, and why they never sleep.

success.text: "After you graduate? Absolutely. Employee number four is yours."

failure.text: "Not yet. Maybe after the next round." They say it nicely.

choices.label: Keep your head down
choices.text: One founder per lab is plenty. You inherit the whiteboard they no longer have time for.

legion.title: Page 13 of the Appendix
text: The four-page short paper on {project} now has a twelve-page statistics appendix. {advisor} is drafting page 13.

choices.label: Keep every page
choices.text: No reviewer will read all twelve pages. No reviewer will find anything to complain about, either.

choices.label: Cut it to the two tests that matter

success.text: The appendix shrinks to one page, and {advisor} gives a rare nod: "Fine. These are the right two."

failure.text: {advisor} restores the other ten pages, with tracked changes and a reading list.

choices.label: Turn it into a lab stats guide
choices.text: The appendix becomes the lab's statistics handbook. Everyone uses it, and {advisor} proudly adds page 14.

legion.title: Significant, or Just Exciting?
text: You show a 2.1-point gain on {project}, and lab meeting cheers. {advisor} waits for the cheering to stop. "Is it significant, or just exciting?"

success.text: p = 0.003. {advisor} allows themselves a very small smile. The lab cheers again, carefully.

failure.text: p = 0.21. It was only exciting, and now you know what to fix.

choices.label: Say "Both, I hope"
choices.text: {advisor} laughs once, which is rare, then asks for the test by Friday.

choices.label: Admit it's just exciting so far
choices.text: "Good. Now make it significant." Your honesty earns a week of goodwill, and a list of seeds to run.

legion.title: The Folder
text: A year in, {advisor} opens a folder of ideas they've collected for years and never shared. "Take one, if any of them speak to you. Or tell me why they're wrong."

choices.label: Pick the one that excites you
choices.text: You pick the fourth one. {advisor} smiles: it was their favorite too, and they never found the time.

success.text: You find the problem with idea three. {advisor} nods: "Good. That's why it's still in the folder."

failure.text: They show you a note from years ago that answers your "flaw". You learn a lot from it.

choices.label: Say you'd rather follow your own
choices.text: "Even better." They close the folder and ask to hear yours.
choices.tip: Find Out What You Are Devoted To

legion.title: Arrive With Answers
text: You bring {advisor} three questions about {project}. They listen, then say kindly: "Next time, bring your best guess for each. It's easier to improve an answer than to start from a question."

success.text: Two of your three guesses are right. You realize you didn't need the meeting for those two.

failure.text: All three guesses are wrong, but now you both know why.

choices.label: Come back tomorrow with answers
choices.text: You return with three answers and one better question. The meeting takes ten minutes.

choices.label: Ask how they would find out
choices.text: They walk you through how they'd look into each one. Halfway through, you see you could have done it yourself.

legion.title: The Regular Visitor
text: A student from another department has come to the last four lab meetings and always orders taro. Nobody remembers inviting them.

choices.label: Ask what they work on
choices.text: They study crowds in train stations. Over taro, you find an idea that needs both your fields.

choices.label: Add them to the order sheet
choices.text: {advisor} adds a fifteenth drink without a word. The visitor looks very grateful.

choices.label: Ask them to present, as the price of tea
choices.text: Their talk on soil chemistry is the best of the semester. Lab meeting runs 30 minutes over, and nobody minds.

legion.title: Perfect Attendance
text: {advisor} notes that you haven't missed an in-person lab meeting in months. "That's real dedication." The bubble tea in your hand may be a factor.

choices.label: Credit your dedication
choices.text: {advisor} nods solemnly. Every labmate in the room looks at your cup.

choices.label: Confess it's the bubble tea
choices.text: "I know. That's why I buy it." The whole lab laughs, and someone raises a cup.

choices.label: Volunteer to present next week
choices.text: To earn your perfect record, you present. Your drink that week comes with extra pudding.

life.title: Lease Renewal
text: Your lease renewal arrives. The rent goes up again, by an amount your stipend has never heard of.
Lease renewal season. Your landlord's letter calls the rent increase "a modest adjustment".

choices.label: Sign it and sigh
choices.text: You sign. Your budget spreadsheet gets a new row called "fewer takeout nights".

success.text: You point out the broken heater and the mystery leak. The increase gets cut in half.

failure.text: Your landlord listens kindly and changes nothing.

choices.label: Move somewhere cheaper
choices.text: Three viewings and a rented van later, you have a cheaper place and a longer commute.

life.title: The Drummer
text: Your roommate's new hobby is drums. They practice every evening from 8 to 10, which used to be your writing time.

choices.label: Buy noise-canceling headphones
choices.text: The drums become a distant thud. You can almost think again.

choices.label: Work late at the lab instead
choices.text: The lab is quiet at night. You start seeing your labmates more than your friends.

success.text: They agree to weekends only. In return, you agree to come to their first gig.

failure.text: They agree, and by Wednesday the drums are back.

choices.label: Join in on bass
choices.text: Your roommate is thrilled. Within a week you have a band and a terrible name for it.

life.title: Moving Week
text: Your lease ends the same week as your deadline for {project}. The boxes are packed, and the paper is not.

choices.label: Move everything in one weekend
choices.text: Two days of stairs and tape. On Monday your back hurts, and so does the draft.

choices.label: Ask the lab to help, buy pizza
choices.text: Four labmates and six pizzas get you moved in one afternoon. You owe everyone a favor.

choices.label: Live out of boxes until the deadline
choices.text: You write the paper sitting on a box labeled KITCHEN, with your laptop on one labeled BOOKS.

life.title: First Snow
text: The first snow of the year. Your walk to the lab takes twice as long, and you arrive looking like a snowman.

choices.label: Work from home today
choices.text: You write all day in warm socks, and it goes surprisingly well.

choices.label: Trudge in anyway
choices.text: You arrive soaked. The lab is empty except for {labmate}, who also trudged in.

choices.label: Build a snowman with the lab
choices.text: It wears a lab badge and holds a sign that says REVIEWER 2. Everyone takes a photo.

life.title: First Warm Day
text: The first warm day of spring. You walk into the lab at 10 am and nobody is there. Everyone is outside on the grass.

choices.label: Join them outside
choices.text: The whole lab lies in the sun, talking about anything but work. It's the best lab meeting of the year.

choices.label: Enjoy the empty lab
choices.text: You have the lab to yourself and get a lot done. It gets a little lonely by lunch.

choices.label: Read papers on the grass
choices.text: You read two papers in the sun. You remember both of them better than usual.

life.title: Lab Thanksgiving
text: {senior} hosts a Thanksgiving potluck for everyone in the lab who can't fly home.

choices.label: Bring a dish you can actually cook
choices.text: Your dish is gone in ten minutes. Several people ask for the recipe.

choices.label: Bring a store-bought pie
choices.text: Nobody judges the pie, and it's the first dish to run out.

choices.label: Stay home and write
choices.text: You get a good writing day. The group chat fills with photos of food.

choices.label: Cook something ambitious
choices.text: Your dish is the talk of the evening. People from two other labs show up just to try it.

life.title: Lunar New Year
text: {labmate} invites the lab over to make dumplings for Lunar New Year.

choices.label: Fold dumplings until midnight
choices.text: Your first dumplings look like modern art. By the fortieth, they look like dumplings.

choices.label: Come for dinner, leave early
choices.text: You eat a lot of dumplings and are home by nine.

choices.label: Send wishes and keep working
choices.text: You send a red envelope emoji to the group chat, then watch the dumpling photos roll in.

life.title: Home for the Holidays
text: Home for winter break. Over dinner, a relative asks when you'll graduate. Everyone stops eating to hear the answer.

choices.label: Give a confident date
choices.text: "Two more years." Everyone is pleased. You will hear this date again next year.

success.text: Your explanation lands. An aunt says it sounds like a startup with no money, which is fair.

failure.text: Ten minutes in, someone asks if you could just finish early.

choices.label: Ask about your cousin's new job
choices.text: The table turns to your cousin. You get a quiet second helping of dessert.

life.title: The Printer
text: You explain your research to your relatives over the holidays. They listen carefully, then ask if you can fix their printer.

success.text: You fix it in five minutes. You are now the family's AI expert and IT department.

failure.text: Two hours later, the printer prints one page and stops forever. Nobody blames you, out loud.

choices.label: Explain your research again
choices.text: Second try: "I help computers understand people." That one sticks.

choices.label: Recommend a new printer
choices.text: They buy a new one online, and you end up setting it up anyway.

life.title: A Cat Named Baseline
text: A shelter near campus posts a photo of a grumpy gray cat named Baseline. Baseline needs a quiet home with someone who works from home a lot.

choices.label: Adopt Baseline
choices.text: Baseline inspects the apartment and moves in by sitting on your printed draft.

choices.label: Foster for a month first
choices.text: Baseline arrives on a trial basis. Baseline does not seem to know it's a trial.

choices.label: Not with these deadlines
choices.text: You close the tab. Baseline finds a home with fewer deadlines a week later.

life.title: The Trial Ends
text: The foster month is over. Baseline has claimed your desk chair and your favorite sweater.

choices.label: Make it official
choices.text: You sign the papers. Baseline celebrates by knocking a pen off your desk.

choices.label: Return Baseline to the shelter
choices.text: The shelter finds Baseline a family within a week. Your chair is yours again, and a little too empty.

life.title: Guest Speaker
text: Halfway through your video update at lab meeting, Baseline sits on your keyboard and blocks the camera. After that, nobody asks about your results, only the cat's name.

choices.label: Introduce Baseline properly
choices.text: Baseline gets a round of applause. Your results get a follow-up meeting.

choices.label: Close the door and carry on
choices.text: Baseline meows through the rest of your update. Your slides have never had a louder audience.

choices.label: Make Baseline the lab mascot
choices.text: By Friday, Baseline is the lab's Slack icon, and {labmate} is printing stickers.

life.title: Submitted by Baseline
text: You leave a half-written peer review open and go make tea. Baseline walks across the keyboard. The review is now submitted, with a score of 1 and the comment "jjjjjjjjjjjjjjj;".

choices.label: Email the area chair and confess

success.text: The area chair reopens it and writes back, "Please thank the cat for its time."

failure.text: The area chair reopens it three days later. You rewrite the whole review over the weekend.

choices.label: Edit the review before the deadline
choices.text: The system still allows edits. Baseline's version stays in the history log forever.

choices.label: Leave it. Baseline has a point.
choices.text: Somewhere, an author gets the shortest review of their life. You and Baseline sleep well.

life.title: Where You Work
text: Your parents visit for a week and want to see "where you work". You think about your desk and its collection of empty coffee cups.

choices.label: Give them the full lab tour
choices.text: They meet your labmates and take a photo of your name on the door.

choices.label: Show them the nice library
choices.text: The library is beautiful and dignified. Your parents assume your desk looks like this.

choices.label: Skip campus, show them the city
choices.text: You spend the week on good food and long walks. They still don't know what you do, and nobody minds.

life.title: "So What Do You Do?"
text: A dating-app match asks what you do. You type "PhD student", and the conversation ends there.
Your dating-app match asks what you do. You say "PhD." They reply "oh" and are never heard from again.

success.text: A new match asks a follow-up question, then another. You have a coffee date on Saturday.

failure.text: "So you're the reason my phone autocorrects everything?" That one ends too.

choices.label: Delete the app, go to trivia night
choices.text: Your friends' team wins on a history-of-computing question that you answered.

choices.label: Put the phone down and work
choices.text: You get some work done. The paper, at least, never asks what you do.

life.title: Twelve Hours Apart
text: Your family is twelve time zones away. When you wake up, they're going to bed. When they wake up, you're debugging.

choices.label: Call at 7 am before the lab
choices.text: A sleepy, happy call. Your mom asks if you're eating. You say yes, which is mostly true.

choices.label: Call at midnight after work
choices.text: Their breakfast is your midnight dinner, and the call runs long.

choices.label: Trade voice messages
choices.text: The conversation stretches over a whole day, one message at a time. It's nearly as good as a call.

life.title: Same Day
text: The same day {paper} is rejected from {venue}, your undergrad friend posts about their second promotion this year.

choices.label: Send a sincere congratulations
choices.text: You mean it, mostly. They write back, "Your stuff is way cooler though."

choices.label: Mute the group chat for a day
choices.text: You take a day off from everyone's good news. Tomorrow you'll be happy for them.

choices.label: Congratulate them, invite them to dinner
choices.text: They pay, to celebrate, and you talk about everything except reviews.

life.title: The Wedding Weekend
text: Your close friend's wedding is the same weekend as your submission deadline for {project}. The invitation has been on your fridge for months.

choices.label: Go and enjoy every minute
choices.text: You dance badly and toast well. On Monday you are behind and happy about it.

choices.label: Go to the ceremony, skip the party
choices.text: You hug the couple after the vows and catch the last train home to write.

choices.label: Send a gift and a video toast
choices.text: Your video toast plays between dinner and dessert. You watch the replay at 2 am, still writing.

life.title: Black Screen
text: The week before your deadline for {project}, your laptop makes a soft clicking noise and never turns on again.

success.text: Your nightly backup has everything up to last night. You lose one paragraph and zero sleep.

failure.text: Your last backup is from March, when the paper was still an outline.

choices.label: Rebuild from Git and Overleaf
choices.text: The code is on Git and the paper is on Overleaf. The figures were only on your desktop.

success.text: {labmate} hands over a slow laptop covered in stickers. It runs, and you owe them big.

failure.text: {labmate}'s laptop is from 2015 and needs updates for a day before it does anything.

life.title: Cracked
text: On the first morning in {city}, your phone slips out of your hand on the convention center stairs. The screen is now a spider web.

choices.label: Tape it and carry on
choices.text: The tape covers the cracks and half the conference app. You navigate by asking strangers.

choices.label: Find a repair shop in {city}
choices.text: The repair shop is two hours across town. You get a new screen and miss the morning session.

choices.label: Go phone-free for the trip
choices.text: Without a phone, you talk to everyone at the coffee breaks. It's the best conference you've had.

life.title: Free Pizza
text: A seminar on medieval tax records is offering free pizza. You have no interest in medieval tax records, and you go anyway.
There's free pizza at a seminar on bridge corrosion, a topic you know nothing about. You get there early.
A poster in the elevator says "Soil Acoustics Seminar, Free Pizza". You only read the second half.

choices.label: Take two slices and slip out
choices.text: That's lunch sorted, and you're fairly sure nobody saw you leave.

choices.label: Stay for the whole talk
choices.text: The speaker uses a method you've never seen. It might work on your data, too.

success.text: Your question is good. The speaker asks to grab coffee, and now you know someone in a whole other field.

failure.text: Your question was answered on slide 4. You eat a third slice in silence.

life.title: Still Alive
text: The desk plant you bought during orientation has survived a whole year, including a heat wave and your idea of a watering schedule.

choices.label: Repot it into something bigger
choices.text: It grows a new leaf in its new pot the following week.

choices.label: Buy it some friends
choices.text: You buy three more plants, and the lab starts calling your desk the greenhouse.

choices.label: Add it to your acknowledgments draft
choices.text: It goes on the list, between your parents and the GPU cluster.

life.title: Just a Short Run
text: A run to clear your head works better than any meeting this month. {labmate} mentions a half-marathon in three months, with a beginner training plan that is "very gentle".

choices.label: Sign up for the half-marathon
choices.text: You pay the entry fee before you can change your mind. The plan says Tuesday is "easy 5k".

choices.label: Run when you feel like it
choices.text: You run a loop by the river whenever the week gets loud.

choices.label: One run was plenty
choices.text: Your shoes go back in the closet. Your legs thank you, and so does your calendar.

life.title: The Long Run
text: Week six of the training plan says "long run, 16 km, Sunday morning". Your legs have opinions about this, and so does your inbox.

choices.label: Do the long run
choices.text: Sixteen kilometers. You think through a whole paper on the way and forget it by the shower.

choices.label: Swap it for two short runs
choices.text: Two short runs are less heroic, but they still count, more or less.

choices.label: Defer the race to next year
choices.text: You email the organizers. The training plan goes in a drawer, and your Sundays come back.

life.title: Race Day
text: Race day: 21 kilometers and a crowd with handmade signs. At kilometer 15, {labmate} holds one up: "REVIEWER 2 IS RIGHT BEHIND YOU."

success.text: You finish strong and a little teary. The medal goes on your monitor, where visitors can't miss it.

failure.text: You start too fast and walk kilometers 17 to 19. You still finish, and you still get the medal.

choices.label: Run easy and enjoy it
choices.text: You high-five every kid on the course and finish in your slowest time, grinning.

choices.label: Run the last 5 km with {labmate}
choices.text: {labmate} jumps in at kilometer 16, in jeans. You cross the line together, and the photo goes in the lab chat.

life.title: The Kitchen at the Party
text: At a friend's party, you end up talking to someone in the kitchen for an hour. They ask good questions about your research and don't flinch at the word "PhD".

choices.label: Ask for their number
choices.text: They type it into your phone themselves, with a dinosaur emoji. You walk home slower than usual.

success.text: At midnight they're still interested, so you swap numbers on the way out.

failure.text: Somewhere around inter-annotator agreement, they spot a friend across the room.

choices.label: Head home early, deadline tomorrow
choices.text: You go home and write, and the draft gets better. You think about the kitchen conversation all week.

life.title: Saturday Dinner?
text: The person from the party texts: dinner on Saturday? Saturday is also when you'd planned to finish your related-work section.

choices.label: Say yes to dinner
choices.text: Dinner turns into a long walk, then a second date. Related work can wait, and it does.

choices.label: Suggest coffee on Sunday instead
choices.text: Coffee turns into lunch. You're taking it slow, and that suits you both.

choices.label: Say you're swamped this month
choices.text: They say "good luck with it" and mean it. You finish related work on Saturday, alone with a citation manager.

life.title: Meal Prep Era
text: You're in a cooking phase. Sunday is meal-prep day now: 14 identical containers and a spreadsheet of macros you'll never open.

choices.label: Keep the streak going
choices.text: Lentils on Monday, lentils on Friday. You've never had more energy, or more lentils.

choices.label: Cook for the lab on Wednesdays
choices.text: Your curry becomes a lab tradition. {labmate} starts bringing a fork from home.

choices.label: Let the phase end gracefully
choices.text: Sunday is yours again. By Thursday, dinner is cereal, eaten standing up.

choices.label: Go full chef
choices.text: Your containers have garnishes. People from other labs ask whether you take orders.

life.title: An Idea and a Sunburn
text: You go hiking with friends and leave the laptop at home. Near the top, the fix for {project} arrives fully formed, along with a sunburn.

choices.label: Type it into your phone right there
choices.text: You write it at the summit with one bar of signal and a red nose. On Monday, it still makes sense.

choices.label: Call {labmate} from the trail
choices.text: {labmate} picks up on the third try and tests half of it by Monday. Your friends roll their eyes all the way down.

choices.label: Enjoy the view and trust your memory

success.text: On Monday the idea is still there, and the rest has made it better.

failure.text: On Monday you remember the view and the sunburn, but not the idea.

life.title: The PhD League
text: You join an intramural soccer team. Every single player is a PhD student. Half-time talk is about p-values, and the captain picks the lineup with a script.

success.text: You lose every game by at least four goals. It's the best part of your week.

failure.text: In the second game, you sprain an ankle chasing a ball you were never going to reach. The team signs your brace.

choices.label: Cheer from the sideline
choices.text: You hold the snacks and shout encouragement. The team votes you most valuable non-player.

choices.label: Model the team's win probability
choices.text: Your model gives the team a 2% chance. They win anyway, and you update your priors in front of everyone.

life.title: Reviewer 2, Times Six
text: Halloween at the lab. Six people show up as Reviewer 2, each with a red pen and a sign that says "The novelty is limited." Nobody coordinated.

choices.label: Go as Reviewer 2 as well
choices.text: Seven Reviewer 2s. The group photo looks like a very harsh program committee.

success.text: You overrule all six of them with one sticky note. Best costume is yours.

failure.text: Nobody knows what an area chair looks like. Several people think you're a delivery driver.

choices.label: Skip the party, finish a draft
choices.text: You hear the laughter through the wall. The draft gets a page longer and a little grumpier.

milestones.title: Required, Apparently
text: A required course on a topic you will never use again assigns a 40-page problem set every week. Your research sits untouched in another tab.

choices.label: Do the minimum, protect research time
choices.text: You get a solid B-plus. Your project barely noticed the course existed.

choices.label: Take it seriously anyway
choices.text: You learn more than you expected. You also sleep less than you expected.

choices.label: Find an angle that connects to your work

success.text: One lecture hands you a framing your project has been missing, which makes up for the problem sets.

failure.text: You try very hard to make it relevant. It stays very irrelevant.

milestones.title: This Could Be a Paper
text: Your course project comes back with one comment from the instructor: "This could be a paper." It overlaps a lot with {project}.

choices.label: Fold it into {project}
choices.text: Half your pilot is now done, and you got a grade for it too.

success.text: {advisor} reads it that week and suggests a sharper framing. You both leave the meeting excited.

failure.text: {advisor} says "interesting" in the tone that means "later". The report goes into a folder.

choices.label: Keep it as a course project
choices.text: You take the A and move on. Your evenings stay free, at least for now.

milestones.title: Finals, Meet Deadline
text: Your final exam and the deadline for {project} land in the same week. Both insist they are the priority.

choices.label: Prioritize the paper
choices.text: The paper goes in and the exam goes okay-ish. You look up your program's minimum passing grade.

choices.label: Prioritize the exam
choices.text: You ace the final. The paper goes in rougher than you would like.

choices.label: Do both by giving up sleep
choices.text: You survive both. You will not remember this week, but your body will.

milestones.title: 80 Papers, Two Weeks
text: The quals reading list arrives: 80 papers, two weeks. Several are 40 pages long. One is a scanned PDF from the 1990s, slightly crooked.

choices.label: Read every single one
choices.text: You read all 80, and your notes are beautiful. Your eyes are not.

choices.label: Split the list with your cohort

success.text: Five of you each summarize 16 papers. Your shared notes get passed down to the next three cohorts.

failure.text: Two people never send their summaries. You read their 32 papers the night before.

choices.label: Read the core 20 deeply, skim the rest
choices.text: You know 20 papers cold and the other 60 by their figures. That's about how your committee read them, too.

milestones.title: The Classic You Never Read
text: {senior} warns you: {committee} always asks about one classic paper from before you were born. You have cited it twice. You have never read it.

choices.label: Read it, plus what it builds on
choices.text: Half of modern NLP turns out to be this paper with more GPUs.

success.text: {senior} still has their notes, including the exact question. You prepare a crisp answer.

failure.text: "Something about the second figure?" That is all {senior} remembers.

choices.label: Read a blog post about it
choices.text: The blog post is confident and slightly wrong. Now you are confident and slightly wrong.

milestones.title: You Passed. Now What?
text: You pass quals. Someone produces a cake, and by 9 pm the lab chat is back to talking about the next deadline.

choices.label: Take the whole weekend off
choices.text: You spend two days without a laptop and remember what your apartment looks like in daylight.

choices.label: Celebrate tonight, work tomorrow
choices.text: You have one good evening with the lab and are back at your desk by morning, a little lighter.

choices.label: Call home with the news
choices.text: Your family asks if this means you are a doctor now. Not yet, but they are proud anyway.

milestones.title: Not a Product
text: At your practice proposal talk, {labmate} raises a hand: "Honest question. Why is this a PhD and not a product?" The room goes quiet.

choices.label: Rebuild the talk around the question
choices.text: You rework the first five slides around what nobody knows yet. The talk gets sharper.

success.text: "A product helps one hospital. The findings explain why it helped, for everyone." {labmate} nods slowly.

failure.text: You describe the product in great detail. Nobody is convinced, including you.

choices.label: Write it down for later
choices.text: It goes on your list of questions to think about. The list is getting long.

milestones.title: Assembling the Committee
text: You need a committee. Your first choice is on sabbatical on another continent, and {committee} has not answered an email since March.

choices.label: Ask the sabbatical one to join by video

success.text: They agree, from nine time zones away. Your dream committee is set.

failure.text: They reply with a lovely photo of a mountain and a polite no.

success.text: {advisor} walks down the hall. {committee} replies within the hour: "Happy to!"

failure.text: Even {advisor} cannot get a reply. You start looking for a fourth option.

choices.label: Pick people who answer email
choices.text: Scheduling will be easy. The names on your committee are a little less famous.

milestones.title: But Does It Scale?
text: Your industry external member returns your proposal draft. Every section has the same comment: "Does this scale?" Including the section on interviewing 12 nurses.

choices.label: Add a scalability section
choices.text: You add two pages on deploying to a million users. Your external member is delighted, and {advisor} is puzzled.

success.text: "Twelve nurses tell us what a million logs can't." Your external member writes that down.

failure.text: They nod thoughtfully and ask, "Sure, but does it scale?"

choices.label: Reply "Yes" and move on
choices.text: It works for now. You have a feeling the question will be back on proposal day.

milestones.title: Crossfire
text: Ten minutes into your committee meeting, {committee} and your external member start arguing about where your thesis should go. You are still on slide 3.

choices.label: Make the case for your own direction

success.text: You lay out where you want to go and why. They both stop, then agree with you, which surprises everyone.
success.tip: Find Out What You Are Devoted To

failure.text: You try. Now they are both arguing with you instead, which is at least unifying.

choices.label: Let them argue it out
choices.text: They go for 40 minutes. You take notes and leave with two theses' worth of feedback.

success.text: {advisor} steps in with a compromise, and the meeting gets back on track. You owe them one.

failure.text: {advisor} joins the argument, on a third side.

milestones.title: Everything Connects
text: Each of your papers made sense on its own. The proposal needs them to tell one story. Right now they tell three, plus an awkward silence.

choices.label: Trace each paper back to one gap
choices.text: You find the thread: each paper fixes a limitation the last one exposed. Chapter 1 almost writes itself.

choices.label: Draw one diagram that links them

success.text: With three boxes and two arrows, it is suddenly obvious that this is one thesis.

failure.text: You end up with fourteen boxes and arrows in every direction. It looks like a subway map.

choices.label: Leave the odd paper out
choices.text: Two papers tell a clean story; the third becomes an appendix. It stings a little.

milestones.title: Five Calendars
text: You need one two-hour slot when five busy people are all free. The scheduling poll comes back with a single green cell: a Friday at 7:30 am.

choices.label: Book the 7:30 am slot
choices.text: You book it before anyone changes their mind. Everyone will arrive with coffee and low expectations.

choices.label: Ask one member to move a meeting

success.text: They move a meeting, and you get a civilized 2 pm slot.

failure.text: They can't. Meanwhile someone else books Friday, and the poll now has zero green cells.

success.text: {advisor} sends one email. Four replies arrive within the hour, all saying yes.

failure.text: {advisor} replies-all with their own availability, which is also only Friday at 7:30 am.

milestones.title: Margins, Again
text: The graduate school rejects your thesis formatting for the fourth time. This round: page numbers on landscape pages are 0.1 inches too low.

choices.label: Fix exactly what they asked
choices.text: You move the page numbers. Approval comes back with a new note about table caption fonts.

success.text: The template compiles on the first try. The office approves it the same day.

failure.text: The template breaks every figure. You spend two days putting them back.

choices.label: Visit the formatting office in person
choices.text: The office is open Tuesdays from 10 to 11. The reviewer fixes everything with you in ten minutes, three rounds too late.

milestones.title: Just One More Chapter
text: {committee} reads your draft and suggests "just one more chapter" on future directions. Your defense is a few weeks away.

choices.label: Write the chapter
choices.text: You write twenty pages in ten days. It is actually good, and you are actually tired.

success.text: You propose a focused five-page section instead. {committee} agrees and seems impressed by the pitch.

failure.text: {committee} agrees to something shorter. Their idea of shorter is 18 pages.

success.text: {advisor} suggests a closing slide on future work instead, and {committee} agrees.

failure.text: {advisor} loves the idea. Now two people want the chapter.

milestones.title: Still Under Review
text: {paper} is still under review at {venue}. The decision is due in the middle of your defense prep, and your defense date depends on it.

choices.label: Refresh the portal every hour
choices.text: The portal does not change. Your stress level does.

choices.label: Write the thesis as if it's accepted
choices.text: The last chapter assumes the best. Writing it calms you more than refreshing ever did.

choices.label: Plan a backup with {advisor}
choices.text: You map out what happens if it's rejected. It isn't fun, but you sleep better, and {advisor} seems reassured too.

milestones.title: Slide 2
text: Your defense begins. Slide 2 is on the big screen, and "Dissertation" is spelled "Dissertaiton". Everyone has seen it.

choices.label: Laugh it off and keep going

success.text: "Clearly it needed one more revision." The room laughs, and the tension is gone.

failure.text: Your joke lands in silence. You click to slide 3 a little too fast.

choices.label: Pause and fix it live
choices.text: Fifteen seconds of typing in front of five professors feels like an hour. {committee} says, "We've all done it."

success.text: You forget about it by slide 4. Nobody mentions it, probably.

failure.text: You think about it for all 60 slides.

milestones.title: The Question You Prepared For
text: Ten minutes in, {committee} interrupts with exactly the question you spent all last week preparing for. You have a backup slide for it: slide 47.

choices.label: Jump to backup slide 47
choices.text: The slide appears, perfectly labeled. {committee} raises an eyebrow, impressed.

success.text: You answer without notes, point by point. The committee exchanges a look that means "ready".

failure.text: You forget the third point, the best one. It is on slide 47.

choices.label: "I'll come back to that at the end"
choices.text: Now you have something to look forward to in the Q&A.

milestones.title: No Signal
text: Five minutes before your defense, the projector says "No Signal". You have tried three adapters. The committee is arriving.

success.text: Your backup PDF on a USB stick works. The fonts are slightly off; everything else is fine.

failure.text: The room's computer wants to install 40 minutes of updates. You start late and flustered.

choices.label: Send {labmate} for another adapter
choices.text: {labmate} sprints across the building and returns, out of breath, with the right one. You owe them lunch.

choices.label: Give the talk at the whiteboard

success.text: You explain five years of research with one marker. The committee calls it the clearest talk they've seen all year.

failure.text: You draw Figure 3 from memory. It is not Figure 3.

milestones.title: You're Frozen
text: {committee} joins your defense by video from a conference hotel. Their picture freezes every few minutes, always mid-question, mouth open.

choices.label: Repeat every answer twice
choices.text: They hear everything because you say everything twice. Your voice gives out right before the last slide.

choices.label: Suggest they switch to audio only

success.text: With audio only, everything works. {committee} thanks you for the fix.

failure.text: They turn off video and unmute a hotel lobby. Everyone hears a suitcase.

choices.label: Let {advisor} relay their questions
choices.text: {committee} types questions into the chat, and {advisor} reads them aloud. It's slow, but nothing freezes.

milestones.title: Congratulations, Doctor
text: Between "Congratulations, Doctor" and commencement sit 14 pages of minor revisions. The graduate school's filing deadline is this Friday.

choices.label: Address all 14 pages properly
choices.text: You answer every comment and fix every figure. The final thesis is the best version of your work.

choices.label: Fix what matters, explain the rest

success.text: Your response letter is so clear that the committee signs off in a day.

failure.text: {committee} replies: "Please address all comments." All 14 pages it is.

choices.label: Recruit {labmate} to proofread with you
choices.text: The two of you spend a weekend on it, with a lot of snacks. You file on Thursday, a day early.

milestones.title: The Hood
text: Commencement. In line to cross the stage, you notice the person behind you trying not to laugh. Your doctoral hood is on backwards.

choices.label: Cross the stage as you are
choices.text: Your family's favorite photo of the day, possibly of the decade. You wave like you meant it.

choices.label: Ask the person behind you to fix it
choices.text: They flip it around in five seconds. It turns out they did the same thing at their master's.

choices.label: Get {labmate} to take a photo first
choices.text: "For the lab chat," {labmate} says. It becomes the chat's icon for the next three years.

milestones.title: The Title Fight
text: You and {advisor} disagree about your thesis title. Yours is accurate and 19 words long. Theirs is four words, and one of them is "Towards".

success.text: You explain what each word is doing, and {advisor} reads it twice and concedes. The title is yours, colon and all.

failure.text: Forty minutes on one word. You win nothing except a strong opinion about colons.

choices.label: Take theirs: "Towards" it is
choices.text: {advisor} is pleased. You'll explain what it means at every talk for a year.

choices.label: Poll the lab with both titles
choices.text: The lab votes for a third title that nobody proposed. Somehow, you and {advisor} both like it.

milestones.title: Satisfactory
text: Your annual review letter arrives. Progress: "Satisfactory." Below it is one long paragraph that uses the word "encourage" four times.
The annual review letter is in. The box says "Satisfactory". The comment says "We encourage continued focus on publication", a sentence with layers.

success.text: {senior} has read dozens of these. "Encourage" means "submit something this year". You leave with a plan.

failure.text: {senior} reads it, frowns and says "Huh." Now two people are worried.

choices.label: Ask {advisor} what it really means
choices.text: "Keep going, just faster." It's blunt and a little scary, but now you know what the paragraph meant.

choices.label: Decide Satisfactory is fine and file it
choices.text: You file the letter and get back to work. The paragraph stays unread, and so does whatever it meant.

milestones.title: New Requirements
text: The program updates its course requirements. Students admitted before the change are "strongly encouraged" to take the new methods course. You read that sentence three times, looking for a loophole.

choices.label: Take the course
choices.text: Ten weeks of problem sets. Week six exposes a flaw in your analysis that a reviewer would have found first.

choices.label: Petition to keep the old rules

success.text: Your petition is polite and quotes the handbook's own page numbers. Approved in a week.

failure.text: The petition goes to a committee that meets once a semester. You take the course while you wait.

success.text: {advisor} sets up an independent study that is mostly your own project. The program accepts it.

failure.text: {advisor} thinks the course would be good for you. Now the encouragement comes from two directions.

milestones.title: The Acknowledgments
text: Chapter 3 took you a week. The acknowledgments have taken two, and you're on draft six. You keep remembering one more person who once fixed your code.

choices.label: Thank everyone, by name
choices.text: It runs to three pages. Your labmates find their names and pretend they didn't look, and your parents read it twice.

choices.label: Keep it to one honest paragraph
choices.text: It's done by lunch. You probably forgot someone, and they'll probably forgive you.

choices.label: Add one joke for the lab

success.text: One line about the coffee machine. Your committee skips it; your labmates will quote it for years.

failure.text: The joke needs a footnote to explain it. You delete it at 2 am, along with an hour of sleep.

research.title: Scooped?
text: An arXiv alert, two weeks before your deadline: a new paper from {biglab} does almost exactly what {project} does, with nicer figures.
{labmate} drops a link in the lab chat: "isn't this yours??" It is. Someone else's version of {project}, posted two weeks before your deadline.

choices.label: Read it line by line tonight

success.text: Page 7: they test on one benchmark and never ask whether people trust the outputs. That gap is yours, if you move fast.

failure.text: They use your datasets and even run your ablation. It really is your paper, only posted first.

success.text: Ten minutes later, your advisor replies: "Breathe. They miss something important. Let's talk tomorrow." You breathe.

failure.text: The reply comes the next afternoon: "Hm. That is close." Nothing else.

choices.label: Close the laptop, take a walk
choices.text: You walk for an hour. The paper is still there when you get back, but now you can read it without panicking.

research.title: Now What?
text: Decision time for {project}. The other paper is already making the rounds, and your deadline hasn't moved.

choices.label: Build the paper around the gap
choices.text: You cite them in the first paragraph, then show what they missed. The paper ends up sharper than before.

success.text: You reframe the paper, compare fairly and cite them generously. Now it reads like a follow-up.

failure.text: Four rewrites of the intro later, it still reads as "like theirs, but later".

choices.label: Rush to submit first
choices.text: You cancel everything. The plan: submit first, polish later.

choices.label: Pivot to a new angle
choices.text: You keep the code and the data and go back to the whiteboard. It stings for a while, then it starts to be fun.

research.title: Concurrent Work
text: The sting has faded. Your related work now has a paragraph that begins "Concurrent with our work", and honestly, it reads well.

success.text: The first author replies within the hour. They were just as worried about you. You agree to compare notes.

failure.text: They reply politely and promise to "keep in touch". Nobody does, and you don't mind.

choices.label: Let it go
choices.text: Two groups had the same idea at the same time. You decide that means it was a good idea.

research.title: Photo Finish
text: Your paper is in, rough edges and all. Now, for the first time, you read the other paper slowly.

choices.label: Draft the comparison you skipped
choices.text: You write one careful page on how the two papers differ, so you're ready when reviewers ask.

choices.label: Sleep for most of a weekend
choices.text: Eleven hours, then ten. The field did not move on without you.

choices.label: Post a preprint with a note
choices.text: Your preprint goes up with a line on concurrent work. People start citing the two papers together.

research.title: The New Angle
text: A month after the pivot, {project} asks a question the other paper never did. You check arXiv twice a day, and so far nobody else has asked it.

success.text: To your surprise, it's a better paper than the one you lost.

failure.text: It's a different paper, about as good as the old one. At least nobody else has written it.

choices.label: Reuse what survived
choices.text: Half the old code still runs, and the data still works. The pivot costs less than it felt like.

research.title: Beaten Zero-Shot
text: {biglab} releases {model} the week before your deadline. Zero-shot, with no training at all, it beats the system you spent months fine-tuning.

choices.label: Add it as a baseline
choices.text: Three days of API calls get you a new row in Table 2. Your system loses, but the comparison is honest.

choices.label: Reframe: where does it still fail?

success.text: It still fails on the cases your paper cares about most, and those failures become your new contribution.

failure.text: It fails less often than you hoped. The reframe eats a week and half your intro.

choices.label: Pretend you didn't see it
choices.text: Out of sight, out of Table 2. Reviewers, unfortunately, have also seen it.

research.title: No README
text: The baseline you have to compare against won't reproduce. Its repo has no README, one script called run2_final.sh, and requirements from three years ago.

success.text: You find a missing flag buried in a shell script. The numbers now match within half a point.

failure.text: A week later you're still five points short. You report what you got and explain why.

choices.label: Email the authors
choices.text: You send a polite email with three specific questions and get no reply, not even an out-of-office. For now, you use their published numbers.

choices.label: Report their published numbers
choices.text: You add a footnote: "numbers from the original paper." It's standard practice, and some reviewer will still ask.

research.title: Re: Missing Hyperparameters
text: A reply to an email you sent almost a year ago: "Sorry for the delay! Learning rate 3e-5, and we used the dev set for early stopping." Your paper has long since moved on.

choices.label: Rerun it, for closure
choices.text: It reproduces on the first try. You feel oddly at peace.

choices.label: Add the details to your repo
choices.text: Your README now documents their baseline better than theirs does. Strangers start starring your repo.

choices.label: Reply "Thanks!" and archive it
choices.text: Inbox minus one. Some future student will find this thread and weep with joy.

research.title: Same Name, Different Model
text: You rerun last month's evaluation through the {biglab} API. Every number has moved by two points. Same model name, no announcement.

choices.label: Rerun everything on the new version
choices.text: After two days of reruns, the tables agree with each other again, until the next silent update.

choices.label: Report the version and date
choices.text: You add a footnote with the exact version string and access date. Reviewers like that kind of thing.

choices.label: Switch to a pinned open model

success.text: The weights sit on your own disk now, and the numbers finally stop moving.

failure.text: The open model needs four GPUs you don't have. After a week, you're back on the API.

research.title: Scheduled Maintenance
text: IT announces cluster maintenance, Monday through Friday. Your deadline is Saturday.
The cluster is down for "planned upgrades". The plan did not include your deadline.
The cluster status page has said "almost done" for two days. Your deadline has said "Friday" the whole time.

success.text: A friend at another school lends you their reservation for the weekend. You owe them a very nice dinner.

failure.text: Everyone you know has the same deadline. Every cluster you know is full.

choices.label: Shrink the experiments to fit
choices.text: You run a smaller model with fewer seeds on your laptop. The results are real, if a little thin.

choices.label: Write the paper while you wait
choices.text: No GPUs, so you write. It turns out the intro was the real bottleneck.

research.title: The Queue
text: There are {roll:300-500} jobs ahead of yours in the GPU queue.
Your job's estimated start time is "in 4 days". This morning it was "in 3 days".
Someone has reserved every GPU on the cluster until Sunday for a job named test.

choices.label: Wait it out
choices.text: On day four, it starts. On day five, it finishes. You feel like you survived something.

success.text: They share. You now owe them coffee for a month, which is a fair price.

failure.text: "Sorry, my deadline is Friday too." Fair enough, if a little awkward.

choices.label: Shrink the experiment
choices.text: With fewer seeds and a smaller model, it runs tonight. Reviewers may notice.

choices.label: Submit at 3 am instead
choices.text: At 3 am the queue is yours alone. Your job starts before your tea goes cold.

research.title: Out of Memory at 99%
text: Your job ran for three days. At 99%, it died: out of memory.
Three days of training. The log ends at step 9,900 of 10,000 with one word: killed.
The progress bar reached 99%. Then the job died, and took the last checkpoint with it.

choices.label: Add checkpointing, then rerun
choices.text: Three more days, but this time you save every hour. Future you says thanks.

choices.label: Halve the batch size and pray

success.text: It finishes, barely, with 200 MB to spare.

failure.text: This time it dies at 98%.

choices.label: Lie on the lab floor
choices.text: {labmate} steps over you without comment. It's a lab tradition.

research.title: It Has Seen the Test Set
text: You paste the first half of a test example into {model}. It completes the rest word for word, including the typo.

choices.label: Build a clean test split
choices.text: You write new examples dated after the model's training cutoff. The scores drop, and now they mean something.

success.text: You add a section on how much the model has memorized. It may be the most interesting part of the paper.

failure.text: It's interesting, but it swallows the paper. After a two-week side quest, the main story is thinner.

choices.label: Note it in Limitations
choices.text: One honest sentence. Reviewer 2 will quote it back to you.

research.title: Too Good to Be True
text: You change one line, a flag you'd forgotten existed, and every metric jumps five points. Nothing in your method explains why.

success.text: It's real: the old config was silently cutting off long inputs. The gain holds across seeds, and now you can explain it.

failure.text: It's a bug: the new line leaked test labels into training. You revert, a little sadder and much safer.
failure.tip: Hold Yourself to a High Standard

choices.label: Rerun with five more seeds
choices.text: Three seeds agree and two don't. The honest gain is about two points, which is still a gain.

choices.label: Take the five points
choices.text: You update Table 2 and keep writing. A small voice says "too good". You turn the music up.

research.title: The Ablation
text: Your ablation is back. Removing the main component, the one in your paper's title, changes the score by 0.1.

success.text: It's the data-cleaning step you added for convenience. You rebuild the paper around it, and it's a better story.

failure.text: Every part helps a little and nothing helps a lot. Two weeks of ablations leave you with no clear story.

choices.label: Reframe as an analysis paper
choices.text: "What Actually Matters?" is a less flashy title, and a more honest paper.

choices.label: Move it to the appendix
choices.text: It becomes Table 9 in Appendix D. Nobody reads Appendix D, except Reviewer 2.

research.title: The Baseline Wins
text: Months of work, and the clever method loses to the simple baseline on every dataset. Publish it anyway?

success.text: You write a clear, careful paper on why the simple thing wins. {labmate} calls it the most useful thing they've read all year.

research.title: The Nurses' Station

research.title: One Sentence

choices.text: Week eight: approved, at 4:58 pm on a Friday. You print the email and pin it above your desk.

success.text: Your protocol was sitting in the wrong reviewer's pile. It's approved by Thursday.

failure.text: "Thank you for your patience." Two more weeks of patience, as it turns out.

choices.text: By week eight you've read twenty papers and drafted the analysis plan, so the wait doesn't feel wasted.

research.title: Three No-Shows
text: You booked the room and bought snacks. Three participants in a row don't show up.

choices.text: You send a reminder the day before and another an hour before. Next week, everyone shows up.

choices.text: The snacks are good, and rebooking only takes an afternoon.

success.text: Just enough people show up this time: five sessions in one day, and a lot of good data.

failure.text: Everyone shows up this time, at once. You run two sessions in parallel, badly.

research.title: A Matter of Type
text: Your participant spends the whole hour on your interface's fonts. "Is this a sans-serif? It feels very sans-serif."

choices.label: Steer them back to the task

success.text: A gentle "great point, and what about this part?" works. You get the last 20 minutes back.

failure.text: They agree, then mention the font twice more.

choices.label: Let them talk; take notes
choices.text: Half your notes are about letter spacing. One line, about where the eye lands first, ends up in your design implications.

research.title: Real Participants
text: Your pilot participant was {labmate}, who finished every task in four minutes. Your first real participant takes forty and never finds the Submit button.

choices.label: Redesign the tasks now
choices.text: After two days of rework, the next sessions finally measure what you meant them to.

choices.label: Keep going; it's a finding too

success.text: "Usability barriers" becomes its own section of the paper.

failure.text: Half your sessions test the tasks, half test the button. It's two messy studies in one.

choices.label: Pilot again with an outsider
choices.text: A friend from another department tries it and can't find the button either. Now you know for sure.

research.title: Mid-Session Crash
text: Twenty minutes into the session, your prototype freezes and quits with an error. The participant looks at you kindly.

success.text: It's back in thirty seconds. You make a joke about live demos, they laugh, and the session goes on.

failure.text: It crashes again at minute 25. You finish the session by sketching the screens on paper.

choices.label: Switch to a paper mock-up
choices.text: The paper version works, and they start drawing on it. Some of the drawings beat your design.

choices.label: End early and fix it tonight
choices.text: You spend the night with the logs. By morning that bug is gone, along with two others you hadn't met yet.

research.title: Access Denied

choices.label: Tether to your phone
choices.text: You get one bar, in one corner of the room. It works as long as nobody moves.

success.text: A nurse knows exactly who to call in IT. You're unblocked by lunch.

failure.text: A ticket is filed. Estimated response: ten business days.

success.text: The offline build runs from a laptop and is faster than the online one, which is a little embarrassing.

failure.text: At 3 am it half-works. The next session runs on the half that works.

research.title: That's Not How a Clinic Works
text: A clinician reads your "realistic scenario" and laughs. "Nobody would see this patient without the chart open. Who wrote this?" You did.

choices.label: Rewrite it with them
choices.text: Thirty minutes later the scenario is realistic, and the clinician is invested in your study.

choices.label: Shadow a clinic shift first
choices.text: After eight hours on your feet, you come back with three better scenarios and very tired legs.

choices.label: Keep it; it's a controlled study
choices.text: Controlled, yes. Reviewers from medicine will have notes.

research.title: The Hallway Conversation
text: Waiting for the elevator, a nurse asks what you're working on. In three minutes, they explain the real problem better than your entire related work section.

choices.label: Take notes right there
choices.text: You miss two elevators and fill four screens of notes.

choices.label: Invite them to your study
choices.text: They say yes, and bring a colleague. Both are better participants than anyone on your list.

success.text: "Sure, if you bring coffee." You have your first clinical collaborator.

failure.text: They laugh: "I barely have time for lunch." But they give you their email, just in case.

research.title: The Bots Found Your Survey
text: Your online survey gets {roll:300-450} responses overnight. Most took under a minute, and every open answer says "Good survey, very nice."

choices.label: Clean it by hand
choices.text: You flag every response that's too fast, too tidy or too nice, and about 30% goes.

choices.label: Add attention checks, relaunch
choices.text: Round two asks: "Select purple." The bots select blue. The humans, mostly, select purple.

success.text: The script checks timing, duplicate answers and pasted text, and catches nearly all the bots in an hour.

failure.text: The script flags half your real participants too. You end up cleaning by hand anyway.

research.title: Neutral on Everything
text: You open the questionnaire results. Every participant picked "Neutral" on every Likert item. Your bar chart is a flat line at 4.

success.text: The story was in the interviews all along. The flat chart shrinks to one sentence.

failure.text: The interviews are polite and vague too. You start to suspect the problem is your tasks.

choices.label: Report "no clear preference"
choices.text: You report the null result in one paragraph. It's the least exciting paragraph in the paper.

choices.label: Fix the questionnaire next time
choices.text: You leave a note for future you: drop the middle option and ask about specific moments.

research.title: [inaudible]
text: The transcripts are back. The best quote of the whole study reads: "The real problem is [inaudible], and that's why we [inaudible]."

choices.label: Re-listen and fix them yourself
choices.text: After ten hours in headphones, you know every participant's laugh and favorite filler word.

choices.label: Ask the participant to recall it

success.text: They reply the same day with an even better version of the quote.

failure.text: No reply. The best quote of the study stays [inaudible] forever.

choices.label: Work with what's legible
choices.text: Most of it is fine. The gaps will show up as a slightly vaguer Findings section.

research.title: Not That Feature
text: Every participant ignores the AI feature your paper is about. They all love the export button you added at 2 am.

success.text: The paper becomes about what people actually wanted, which is more surprising than what you planned.

failure.text: The reframe never quite lands. Is it a paper about export buttons now?

choices.label: Redesign so they find the AI
choices.text: You move the AI feature front and center. In the next round of sessions, they use it.

choices.label: Report both, honestly
choices.text: You write one section on the feature you built and another on the export button they loved.

research.title: A Larger Sample
text: The reviews agree on one thing: "The sample is small." Your 12 clinicians took six months to recruit.

choices.label: Recruit more, however long it takes
choices.text: You reopen recruiting. The paper will be stronger, and much later.

success.text: You write a paragraph on why 12 deep sessions with experts beat 100 shallow ones. It even convinces you.

failure.text: It reads as defensive. You rewrite it twice, and it still reads a little defensive.

success.text: A hospital mailing list does the trick. A hundred survey responses back up your 12 interviews.

failure.text: Eleven responses, three of them from the same person. The survey becomes a footnote.

research.title: Their Bug, Your Win

success.text: They confirm it within a day and post a correction that thanks you by name.

failure.text: "Thanks, we'll look into it." The correction never comes, but at least you know your own numbers are right.

choices.label: Write it up as a short note
choices.text: You write four careful, kind pages on reproducing their result. More people read it than either original paper.

choices.label: Smile and say nothing
choices.text: You tell no one and reread your related work, slowly, with a small private grin.

research.title: Saturated
text: {biglab} releases {model}. Slide 14: {roll:97-99}% on your benchmark, six months after you released it. Your leaderboard is now a list of rounding errors.

choices.label: Build a harder version 2

success.text: It aces your benchmark and stumbles on a lightly reworded copy. That's a short paper right there.

failure.text: It really is that good, on everything you try. You learn a lot about the model, and nothing you can publish.

choices.label: Call it a success
choices.text: Saturated means used. You add "widely adopted" to your CV and close the tab.

research.title: Seed 43
text: Seed 42: your method wins by three points. Seed 43: it loses by one. Seed 44 would rather not get involved.

choices.tip: Hold Yourself to a High Standard

choices.label: Find out why it's so fragile

success.text: The culprit is a warmup schedule that only works on lucky seeds. Once you fix it, the gain holds on all of them.

failure.text: Two days of staring at loss curves. They look like modern art and explain about as much.

choices.label: Report seed 42
choices.text: Everyone uses 42, you tell yourself. Reviewer 2 has heard that one before.

research.title: Price Update

choices.text: You keep the experiments that answer the question and drop the ones that only decorate it.

failure.text: "Budgets are budgets." Your advisor suggests you get creative. You were afraid of that.

choices.label: Move to an open model
choices.text: After a week of setup, every run costs only electricity and a lot of patience.

research.title: Works in the Demo

failure.text: Every failure fails in its own way. You now have 400 rows of sadness in a spreadsheet.

research.title: Just in Case

research.title: Ten Times Easier

failure.text: The bigger question is bigger than you thought. Your scope doubles, and so does your to-do list.

research.title: Grading Its Siblings

failure.text: Interesting, but three papers found it last month. It shrinks to a footnote.

research.title: Copy x3

failure.text: Your replacement has 800 examples and a bad attitude. You end up switching to an open dataset anyway.

research.title: Anything Else?

failure.text: Silence again. Their name goes on a list you call "someday".

choices.label: Catch them after a hospital talk

research.title: One Participant

choices.label: Run the session anyway
choices.text: A great participant, full of stories about your advisor at your age. You get data and gossip.

success.text: One post in the right forum and your calendar fills up in two days.

failure.text: Forty replies, all from accounts selling followers.

failure.text: "Nothing much." They go quiet again, now slightly self-conscious.

research.title: Can I Keep It?

choices.text: You fix the worst bugs and answer their emails. Their real-world use becomes the best part of the paper.

choices.label: Add a field deployment
choices.text: It takes an IRB amendment and a month of real use. The paper gets much stronger, and much later.

research.title: Who Goes First

failure.text: They're polite and unconvinced. The thread grows to 31 emails.

success.text: Your advisor and theirs talk for ten minutes. You stay first author. Nobody tells you what was said.

failure.text: Your advisor proposes co-first authorship and a footnote. The clinician takes it, and you try to be gracious.

research.title: Legal Review

failure.text: They have 14 comments on the template, numbered and lettered. Some have sub-letters.

choices.label: Strike that one, accept the rest

failure.text: They counter your counter. A meeting is scheduled to plan the meeting about it.

research.title: Round Three

failure.text: "We'll have to stop at 14." Your study just became a lot more qualitative.

research.title: 412 Sticky Notes

choices.label: Photograph and code them on screen
choices.text: On screen the notes are searchable and somehow less inspiring. The themes come out tidy and a little flat.

choices.label: Ask the participants to vote on themes

success.text: Eight participants come back and sort the notes with you. Their themes beat yours.

failure.text: Two participants come back. They mostly vote for "lunch?".

research.title: That's Not What I Meant
text: You share your findings with a participant, as promised. They reply within the hour: "That's not what I meant. At all." Your favorite theme is built on their quote.

choices.label: Revise the theme
choices.text: After two days of rereading transcripts, the new theme is less striking and much more accurate.

choices.label: Add their correction as a quote
choices.text: Their reply goes into the paper next to your reading, and a reviewer praises the paper as "reflexive".

success.text: After a call, they agree: "Okay, I did kind of mean that."

failure.text: The call ends with each of you more sure you're right.

research.title: The Pager Saga
text: Twenty minutes in, your interviewee starts telling the story of the clinic's old pager system. It has villains and a twist, and it's nowhere on your interview guide.

choices.label: Let them talk
choices.text: They talk about pagers for forty minutes, and somewhere in there is the best quote about workarounds you've ever heard.

success.text: "That's fascinating, and does it connect to..." It does. You finish the guide on time.

failure.text: You steer back. They steer to the fax machine.

choices.label: Book a follow-up for the story
choices.text: The extra hour next week costs you an afternoon and gets you a friend in the clinic.

research.title: 0 Bytes
text: You open the screen recording of your best session, the one where everything clicked: 0 seconds, 0 bytes. The audio is fine.

choices.label: Rebuild it from your notes
choices.text: You spend an evening stitching the audio and your notes together. It's mostly right, you think.

choices.label: Ask the participant for a follow-up

success.text: They're happy to do it again, and even sharper the second time.

failure.text: They're away for a month. You make do with the audio.

choices.label: Drop the session
choices.text: Your best session becomes one sentence in Limitations. It's the rigorous choice, and it stings a little.

research.title: Can You Tell?
text: The manipulation check is in: participants can't tell the AI condition from the no-AI condition. Half think both had AI. A few think neither did.

choices.label: Redesign the conditions
choices.text: After a new pilot and another round of sessions, the study tests what it says it does.

success.text: You rewrite the framing around a new finding: people can't tell when AI is helping.

failure.text: Reviewers will see a failed manipulation, and so do you. The reframe doesn't hold.

choices.label: Make the AI more visible
choices.text: You add a sparkle icon and the word "AI" in bold. Now everyone notices, and some notice too much.

research.title: Too Clever
text: You pilot your survey on {advisor}. Your attention check is so clever that {advisor} fails it, then argues for ten minutes that it was ambiguous.

choices.label: Simplify it
choices.text: "Select 'Strongly agree' for this item." It isn't clever, and your advisor passes it.

choices.label: Keep it and call it rigor
choices.text: Rigor! It filters out bots and, apparently, professors. Your advisor will remember this.

choices.label: Add a second, easier one
choices.text: Two checks: one for bots, one for humans. The survey grows by a page.

research.title: Basically 24
text: Your counterbalanced design needs 24 participants, one for each order. You have 23. Participant 24 cancelled this morning, very apologetically.

choices.label: Recruit one more
choices.text: One more flyer and one more week get you participant 24. The design is balanced again.

choices.label: Report the unbalanced order
choices.text: You admit it in one sentence in the method section. A reviewer will count, but you counted first.

success.text: Your advisor laughs, then helps you rerun the analysis with order as a factor, and the result holds.

failure.text: "Is it?" asks your advisor, and waits. You go and find participant 24.

research.title: Soup of the Day
text: Mid-session, your study chatbot answers a clinician's question about discharge notes with a recipe for lentil soup. The clinician reads it carefully. "This actually looks good."

choices.label: Log it and move on
choices.text: A line in your notes: "14:32, soup." The session goes on. Afterward, the clinician asks for the recipe.

choices.label: Pause and fix the prompt
choices.text: Ten minutes of frantic prompt editing while the participant waits. No more soup, for now.

success.text: You find 11 more off-topic replies in the logs, enough for a section on trust.

failure.text: It's one soup. A finding needs more than one soup.

research.title: Thirty Seconds
text: The clinicians like your tool, with one condition: it has to work in the 30 seconds between patients. Right now, logging in takes 40.

choices.label: Redesign for 30 seconds
choices.text: You cut every screen you can. What's left fits in 30 seconds, with a few to spare.

choices.label: Time how long it really takes
choices.text: You spend a day in the clinic with a stopwatch. The real gap is 22 seconds, and now you know where they go.

success.text: You propose a review at the end of the shift instead. They think it over and agree it's better.

failure.text: "There is no other moment," they say, kindly.

research.title: Button, Button, Button
text: A quick accessibility check before the study: the screen reader announces all 23 buttons in your prototype as "button".

choices.label: Fix it all before the study
choices.text: You fix labels, focus order and contrast. It takes a week, and the prototype is better for everyone.

choices.label: Fix the worst three issues
choices.text: The main flow works now. The settings page remains a mystery, read aloud.

choices.label: Note it as a limitation
choices.text: It gets one sentence in Limitations, which is accurate and a little uncomfortable to type.

research.title: Eleven Implications
