success.text: You bond over terrible hotel coffee. They invite you to their lab's reading group.

failure.text: The small talk runs out after the bread basket. Still, they know your face now.

success.text: They push back hard on one detail, and they're right. You leave with a better project.

failure.text: They politely turn to the person on their other side for dessert.

travel.title: Last Talk, Last Day
text: Your talk on {paper} is the last one on the last day of {venue}. The room seats 300. Eleven people came, and four are packing their bags.

choices.label: Give it everything anyway
choices.text: The eleven ask great questions. One of them turns out to be next year's program chair.

choices.label: Cut it to ten minutes
choices.text: You finish early. Everyone makes their flight, and they like you for it.

choices.label: Pull the chairs into a circle

success.text: The talk turns into a discussion. Half an hour later, nobody has left.

failure.text: Two more people leave while you move chairs. The remaining nine have a lovely chat.

travel.title: Minute Twelve
text: Your talk on {paper} is at minute 12 of 15 when the session chair stands up and starts thanking you. Your two best slides are still ahead.

choices.label: Jump to the conclusion
choices.text: You land the last slide in twenty seconds. It's the cleanest summary you've ever given.

success.text: You fit both slides in at double speed. Someone in the front row claps.

failure.text: Nobody follows the last two slides, including you.

choices.label: Say "Find me at the break"
choices.text: Three people do. The coffee break goes better than the talk.

travel.title: Free Socks, One Interview
text: An industry booth is giving away very nice socks. The recruiter behind it asks if you'd like a quick interview while you're there.

success.text: Twenty minutes later you have socks and a second-round slot.

failure.text: You blank on a coding question you'd solve in your sleep. You keep the socks.

choices.label: Take the socks and a business card
choices.text: You leave with good socks and no interview questions.

choices.label: Skip the booth for a talk
choices.text: The talk is about evaluation design, and it's exactly what you needed.

travel.title: Seeing the City
text: You always wanted to see {city}. So far, you have seen the convention center, the hotel, and the hallway between them.

choices.label: Skip a session to explore
choices.text: You find a market and eat something wonderful. The talk you missed is online anyway.

choices.label: Stay for every session
choices.text: You see every talk and meet a lot of people. {city} remains a view from the hotel window.

choices.label: Stay one extra day
choices.text: You stay one more day and finally see {city}. The inbox can wait.

travel.title: Four Minutes
text: The welcome reception opens at 7 pm. By 7:04, the food is gone. You were in line for the coat check.

choices.label: Network on an empty stomach
choices.text: You meet five people and remember two of their names. You are very hungry.

choices.label: Find food with other hungry students
choices.text: Six hungry PhD students find a noodle place nearby. You now have a group chat for the rest of the week.

choices.label: Go back to the hotel
choices.text: You eat room service in bed and fall asleep by nine.

travel.title: The Keynote Spark
text: A keynote at {venue} reframes a problem you've been stuck on. By the end, you have a page of notes and a new project idea.

success.text: They like the idea and suggest a dataset. You promise to follow up, and you mean it.

failure.text: The line to talk to them is forty people deep. You keep your notes.

choices.label: Write it up on the flight home
choices.text: You have four pages by landing, and your seatmate now knows more about your research than your family does.

choices.label: Let it sit in your notes app
choices.text: It joins 140 other ideas in your notes app, some of which are probably good.

travel.title: The Flight Home
text: On the flight home, the passenger next to you coughs for six hours straight. By landing, your throat feels like sandpaper.

choices.label: Take two days off to recover
choices.text: You live on soup and sleep for two days. By Wednesday you're back, mostly human.

success.text: The cold never quite arrives, though the week leaves you tired.

failure.text: It arrives in full. You spend the week on the couch with tissues and a stack of papers you don't read.

choices.label: Work from home in a blanket
choices.text: Your labmates thank you for not bringing it to the lab.

travel.title: The Live Demo
text: Your live demo for {paper} begins. The conference Wi-Fi does not. Forty people watch a loading spinner on the big screen.

choices.label: Run it off your phone's hotspot

success.text: The demo runs on two bars of signal. The audience applauds, mostly for the hotspot.

failure.text: Your phone connects, then dies at 4%. You finish with screenshots.

choices.label: Narrate screenshots like a cooking show
choices.text: "Here's one I prepared earlier." People laugh, then ask good questions.

choices.label: Invite people to try it later
choices.text: Six people find you at the break and try it on a wired connection. Two of them stay for an hour.

travel.title: Student Volunteer
text: Volunteering got you free registration at {venue}. It also got you a STAFF lanyard and a week of carrying microphones to people whose question is "more of a comment".

choices.label: Run microphones in the main hall
choices.text: You hand the mic to three famous people. One of them thanks you by name, reading it off your badge.

choices.label: Swap for the registration desk
choices.text: Everyone passes through. You meet 400 people for eight seconds each, and point 300 of them to the restroom.

choices.label: Skip a shift to see a talk

success.text: Another volunteer covers for you. The talk is great, and you owe them a coffee.

failure.text: The coordinator notices. Your next shift is the 7 am coffee setup.

travel.title: Almost the Same Paper
text: At the poster session, you meet a student from another lab working on almost exactly your problem. You use the same data with different methods, and you both have the same look of mild panic.

choices.label: Propose working together
choices.text: You swap emails and sketch a plan on a napkin. It's either the start of something or a very nice napkin.

choices.label: Race them to the next deadline
choices.text: You both smile and walk away fast. You learned a lot about their method, and your next month got more urgent.

choices.label: Compare notes and stay friendly
choices.text: Two of your dead ends were theirs too. You both save a month and stay in touch, loosely.

travel.title: The Joint Paper
text: Your collaborator from the conference sends a draft that runs their method on your data, and the results beat both of yours. Whose name goes first?

choices.label: Offer them first author
choices.text: They're delighted. The paper goes out, and their lab invites you to visit next spring.

success.text: You agree on co-first authorship with a footnote, and both advisors sign off.

failure.text: Three weeks of polite emails go into one footnote. The paper still goes out, a little late.

choices.label: Take first author, write most of it
choices.text: You write it over two weekends. It's your best draft yet, and you are very tired.

travel.title: Silent Film
text: {venue} plays pre-recorded talks in your session. Yours, for {paper}, starts with no audio. You're in the third row, and every head slowly turns toward you.

choices.label: Narrate it live from your seat

success.text: You talk over your own silent video, perfectly in sync. It's the most memorable talk of the session.

failure.text: You fall two slides behind your own video and never catch up.

choices.label: Ask the AV team to fix it
choices.text: Ten minutes later, the sound works. Your talk plays to a smaller, very patient room.

choices.label: Skip straight to the Q&A
choices.text: You take questions instead. There are only three, because nobody heard the talk.

travel.title: Chair of Session 7B
text: The conference app lists you as chair of Session 7B: "Speech Recognition for Farm Equipment". You have never chaired a session. You are not in this session.

choices.label: Chair it anyway
choices.text: You keep time, ask one question per talk and learn a lot about tractors.

success.text: They fix it within the hour and apologize with a drink voucher.

failure.text: They reply after the session. Nobody chaired it, so the speakers timed each other.

choices.label: Find the real chair
choices.text: You find them at the coffee urn. They had no idea either, so you chair it together.

travel.title: 300 Views
text: The recording of your talk on {paper} is online. It has 300 views. According to the analytics, about 200 of them come from your parents' town.

choices.label: Share it more widely
choices.text: Views climb to 900. A few comments ask good questions, and one asks about your microphone.

choices.label: Call your parents to say thanks
choices.text: They have watched it eleven times, and one of them has a question about slide 9.

choices.label: Watch it yourself, once
choices.text: You count 47 "um"s. It's painful, but your next talk will have fewer.

wellbeing.title: Six Weeks
text: You try to remember your last real day off. It was six weeks ago, and you spent it doing laundry.

choices.label: Take a real day off tomorrow
choices.text: You go for a long walk and never open your email. The work is still there on Monday, and so are you.

choices.label: Plan a long weekend next turn
choices.text: You block it on your calendar and tell three people, so you can't back out.

choices.label: Keep going, it's almost done
choices.text: It is not almost done. It never is, but you do get a lot done this week.

wellbeing.title: The Cabin
text: Your friends rent a cabin by a lake for a week, with no Wi-Fi and one spare bed with your name on it.

choices.label: Go, and leave the laptop home
choices.text: You swim and play cards for seven days. By day four, you've forgotten your own password.

choices.label: Go, but bring the laptop
choices.text: You work mornings on the porch and swim in the afternoons.

choices.label: Stay and work
choices.text: The photos in the group chat look wonderful.

wellbeing.title: The Inbox
text: You open your laptop after the lake: {roll:100-140} unread emails and nine messages from {advisor}. The last one says "Never mind, figured it out."

choices.label: Answer every single one today
choices.text: You reach inbox zero by midnight. The lake already feels like a dream.

choices.label: Read only your advisor's
choices.text: Most of them answered each other. You reply to the last one with a thumbs-up.

choices.label: Mark all as read
choices.text: It feels wonderful. One of them was an invitation to give a talk.

wellbeing.title: Fresh Eyes
text: Back from a week with no laptop, you open {project}. The problem you were stuck on for a month is obvious in ten minutes.

choices.label: Fix it right now
choices.text: Two hours of work and it's solved. You wonder what else a week off could fix.

choices.label: Write down why it was hard to see
choices.text: You write a page on what you missed and why, so you'll spot it next time.

wellbeing.title: It's Going Around
text: A cold is going around the lab. {labmate} sneezes, apologizes, and sneezes again. By Thursday, it's your turn.

choices.label: Stay home and rest
choices.text: Two days of soup and sleep. You come back mostly human.

choices.label: Work from home in a blanket
choices.text: You answer emails under a blanket. Productivity is low, and so is the risk to everyone else.

success.text: You shake it off in a day. Nobody else catches it.

failure.text: It hits harder than expected. Also, {labmate2} now has it.

wellbeing.title: Fully Nocturnal
text: Your sleep schedule is now fully nocturnal. You eat breakfast at 3 pm and do your best work at 2 am.

choices.label: Reset with a 7 am alarm
choices.text: Three groggy days later, you see the sun on purpose.

choices.label: Shift an hour earlier each day
choices.text: By next week, you're eating breakfast at breakfast time.

choices.label: Keep the night shift
choices.text: The cluster is empty at 2 am and your jobs fly. Your labmates forget what you look like.

choices.label: Own it
choices.text: This is your natural habitat. You do the best work of your month by moonlight.

wellbeing.title: A Good Meeting
text: Your meeting with {advisor} about {project} goes unexpectedly well. Thirty minutes in, you remember why you wanted to do this project.

choices.label: Ride the momentum all weekend
choices.text: You put in two long, focused days. You're tired, and the project is moving again.

choices.label: Write down the next three steps
choices.text: Three clear steps go on a sticky note on your monitor, where Monday-you will find them.

choices.label: Celebrate with bubble tea
choices.text: {labmate} joins you. You both agree it's been a good day.

wellbeing.title: Just a Small One
text: {labmate} asks you to join a side project. It would be your fourth. "It's small," they say. They always say that.

choices.label: Say no, kindly
choices.text: They understand right away. You feel lighter than you expected.

choices.label: Say yes
choices.text: Your calendar now has a different color for each project, and you're running out of colors.

choices.label: Offer an hour of feedback instead
choices.text: You give one hour of careful comments. It turns out that's exactly what they needed.

wellbeing.title: The Chair
text: Your lower back has started filing complaints about your office chair. The chair is older than you are.

choices.label: Ask the department for a real chair
choices.text: It takes three emails and a form, but the new chair arrives. Your back sends a thank-you note.

choices.label: Stack books under the monitor
choices.text: Two volumes of an old statistics textbook finally earn their place on your desk.

choices.label: Ignore it
choices.text: Your back does not ignore you.

wellbeing.title: Twenty-Twenty-Twenty
text: After eleven hours of screens, the text on your monitor starts to swim, and blinking doesn't help.

choices.label: Look away every twenty minutes, like the poster says
choices.text: Every twenty minutes, twenty feet, twenty seconds. You get to know the tree outside the window very well.

choices.label: Turn the brightness down and keep going
choices.text: The headache arrives on schedule.

choices.label: Get your eyes checked
choices.text: You get new glasses. The world is sharper, and so are your figures.

wellbeing.title: It's Going Around
text: Half the lab is coughing. The other half is pretending not to hear it.

choices.label: Work from home for a while
choices.text: You miss two lab meetings and zero viruses.

success.text: Your immune system holds. You feel invincible, which is a mistake.

failure.text: Day three: you have it too.

choices.label: Get the flu shot today
choices.text: A sore arm and a smug feeling for a week.

wellbeing.title: Lunch Is a Suggestion
text: You realize that for three weeks, lunch has been crackers from the vending machine, eaten over your keyboard.

choices.label: Meal prep this Sunday
choices.text: You make five containers of something green and feel like an adult.

choices.label: Join the lab for lunch
choices.text: Real food, and gossip about which professor is moving to industry.

choices.label: The crackers are fine
choices.text: The crackers are not fine.

wellbeing.title: The Morning After
text: You hit submit at 4:12 am. At 9:00 there's lab meeting. Your body has questions.

choices.label: Sleep through lab meeting
choices.text: You sleep until noon and apologize on the lab chat. Your advisor replies with a thumbs-up.

choices.label: Go anyway, with three coffees
choices.text: You present your results with great energy and little sense.

wellbeing.title: The Fifth Coffee
text: It's 2 pm and you're holding your fifth coffee. Your hands are doing a small, steady dance.

choices.label: Switch to decaf for a while
choices.text: The first two days are rough. Then you sleep through the night for the first time since September.

choices.label: Make it a sixth
choices.text: You've never written code this fast. Most of it is wrong.

wellbeing.title: The Wrist
text: Your right wrist aches every time you reach for the mouse. It started as a twinge. It's now a whole opinion.

choices.label: Get a split keyboard and a better mouse
choices.text: For a week you type like a toddler. Then the ache is gone.

choices.label: Push through
choices.text: The ache moves up your arm, as if exploring.

choices.label: Try dictating your related work
choices.text: Your laptop transcribes "transformer" as "trans former" forty times. Your wrist gets a rest.

wellbeing.title: The Front Row
text: You fall asleep in a department talk, in the front row, and the speaker notices.

choices.label: Go to bed at ten for the next two weeks
choices.text: It feels like a vacation you didn't have to book.

choices.label: Buy the large coffee from now on
choices.text: You stay awake in talks. You also stay awake at 2 am.

wellbeing.title: The Ankle
text: One bad landing in a pick-up basketball game, and your ankle turns a color you didn't know ankles could be.

choices.label: Rest it properly
choices.text: You keep it iced and up on the couch, and read a lot.

choices.label: Limp to the lab
choices.text: Everyone asks what happened. You tell the story eleven times; it gets better each time.

wellbeing.title: The Three-Day Headache
text: A headache moves in on Monday and is still there on Wednesday, like a labmate who never goes home.

choices.label: Close the laptop at six for a week
choices.text: It leaves on Friday. So does some of the stress.

choices.label: Painkillers and keep going
choices.text: It leaves eventually. It leaves a forwarding address.

wellbeing.title: Pollen Season
text: The trees outside the lab are blooming beautifully, and your sinuses have declared war on all of them.

choices.label: Antihistamines
choices.text: You can breathe. You can also barely keep your eyes open.

choices.label: Tough it out
choices.text: You go through a box of tissues a day. People keep asking if the code is that bad.

wellbeing.title: The Lab Fridge
text: You eat a yogurt from the lab fridge. It had your name on it. It did not have a date on it.

choices.label: Stay home until it passes
choices.text: Two days on the bathroom floor, contemplating your choices.

choices.label: Clean out the lab fridge, for everyone's sake
choices.text: You find things that predate your advisor. The lab is grateful, and slightly scared.

wellbeing.title: Dragged to Dinner
text: At 8 pm, a friend from outside the lab appears at your desk holding your coat. "You said 'next week' three weeks ago. It's next week."

choices.label: Go, and leave the laptop behind
choices.text: Three hours of dumplings and stories that have nothing to do with research. You sleep in the next morning and don't regret it.

choices.label: Go, but only for an hour
choices.text: You have one quick bowl of noodles and go back to the lab feeling a bit better.

choices.label: "Ten more minutes"
choices.text: You finish the section. They leave a takeout box on your desk with a sticky note: "Next week. Really."

wellbeing.title: Somebody Else's Best Paper
text: {labmate} wins a best-paper award. You're truly happy for them. Then, around 11 pm, a small voice asks what exactly you've been doing all year.

choices.label: Ask {labmate} how they did it
choices.text: Over coffee, {labmate} admits the project failed twice before it worked, and their first draft was worse than yours.

choices.label: Work twice as hard this month
choices.text: You out-work the small voice for two weeks. It's still there, and now you're both tired.

choices.label: List three things you did this year
choices.text: The list runs well past three. You read it twice, then go to bed.

choices.label: Read their paper to find the trick
choices.text: There's no trick, just a careful, good paper, and somehow that helps.

wellbeing.title: Ten in a Row
text: Ten gym sessions in a row. The front desk nods at you now, and you've started saying "leg day" without irony.

choices.label: Keep the streak going
choices.text: You keep going to thirteen. Your back stops complaining about the chair, and your calendar starts instead.

choices.label: Bring {labmate} next time
choices.text: {labmate} lasts twenty minutes and is sore for three days. They want to go again, which surprises you both.

choices.label: Reward yourself with a week off
choices.text: You spend a week on the couch. The streak ends at ten, which is still ten.

choices.label: Go for twenty
choices.text: You make it to twenty and feel unstoppable, except around 3 pm.

wellbeing.title: Thrilled to Share
text: Decisions are out for a big conference, and your feed is a wall of "Thrilled to share..." posts. You've been scrolling for forty minutes and stopped reading the titles a while ago.

choices.label: Close the app and go for a walk
choices.text: The trees outside haven't had a paper accepted either, and they seem fine.

choices.label: Like every single one
choices.text: Two hundred likes later, you're a supportive member of the community, and slightly hollow.

choices.label: Mute the word "thrilled"
choices.text: Your feed goes quiet and slightly confusing. You miss a friend's real news and hear about it a week late.

wellbeing.title: The Extra Hour
text: Daylight saving ends and the clocks go back, which gives you one free hour.

choices.label: Spend the hour asleep
choices.text: The best hour of sleep you've had all semester. You wake up almost rested.

choices.label: Spend it on one more experiment
choices.text: The extra hour goes to one more run, which takes three hours. You end up two hours behind.

choices.label: Book a 7 am meeting; it "feels like 8"
choices.text: It does feel like 8, for about a week. Then it feels like 7 again, and the meeting is now recurring.

wellbeing.title: 5 Hours 12 Minutes
text: {labmate} lends you their sleep tracker. After a week, it reports your average: 5 hours 12 minutes. It has also awarded you a badge called "Night Explorer".

choices.label: Set a bedtime alarm and obey it
choices.text: Lights out at 11:30. You lose your late-night hours and find your mornings.

choices.label: Keep wearing it, stop looking at it
choices.text: The data is still collected. It just isn't anyone's problem now.

choices.label: Return it with a note: "broken"
choices.text: {labmate} checks it, finds nothing wrong and gives you a long look.

wellbeing.title: The Lab Couch
text: You nap on the lab couch between runs. Forty minutes later you wake up with your neck stuck at a jaunty angle.

choices.label: Heat pack and slow stretches
choices.text: A slow, careful afternoon. By evening you can check your blind spot again.

choices.label: Work with your head tilted
choices.text: Your monitor looks a bit crooked all day. {labmate} tilts their head in solidarity.

choices.label: Go home and sleep in a real bed
choices.text: Twelve hours later your neck is straight, and your runs have finished without you.

wellbeing.title: The Radiator
text: The radiator in your apartment clanks from 2 to 4 am, every night, like someone is trapped inside with a wrench.

choices.label: Buy earplugs
choices.text: Silence at last. You also sleep through your alarm, twice.

choices.label: Write a polite note to the landlord

success.text: Your note is so well argued that someone comes out the same week. The radiator now hums, gently.

failure.text: The landlord replies that this is normal for an old building, which is true and doesn't help.

choices.label: Use the hours to write
choices.text: You write two hours a night, typing in time with the clanks. The draft grows, and your eyes stop fully opening.

wellbeing.title: Forty Tabs
text: It's 1 am. You're in bed, and your phone has forty arXiv tabs open. Each one is "just the abstract".

choices.label: Leave the phone outside the bedroom
choices.text: You buy an old-school alarm clock. The first three nights feel strange. Then you sleep like you used to.

choices.label: Save them for the morning
choices.text: You bookmark all forty. In the morning you read two, properly. The other 38 join the folder of good intentions.

choices.label: Just one more abstract
choices.text: By 2:40 am you understand a whole new subfield, sadly not yours.

wellbeing.title: Fourteen Hours
text: The weekend after you submit {paper}, you go to bed at 9 pm and wake up at 11 am.

choices.label: Do it again on Sunday
choices.text: Another long night. On Monday you feel like someone just back from vacation.

choices.label: Get up and clean the apartment
choices.text: You find three mugs you thought you'd lost and one you wish you hadn't. The apartment is clean; you are tired.

choices.label: Start planning the next paper
choices.text: By Sunday night you have an outline and a mild headache.

wellbeing.title: For Training Purposes
text: The university offers free ergonomic assessments. The assessor frowns at your desk and photographs your setup "for training purposes".

choices.label: Follow every recommendation
choices.text: It takes a full day and a lumbar pillow shaped like a burrito. Your back feels better by evening.

choices.label: Fix only the monitor height
choices.text: You raise the monitor on the conference proceedings you never read, which finally have a use.

choices.label: Ask them to blur your face
choices.text: They agree. Your posture, unchanged, becomes an anonymous warning in next year's training slides.

wellbeing.title: The Standing Desk
text: Your standing desk arrives. On day one you stand for two hours. On day two it becomes a regular desk, slightly taller.

choices.label: Alternate on a timer
choices.text: You switch every thirty minutes. Your legs complain for a week, then stop.

choices.label: Use it as a shelf for printed papers
choices.text: It holds 300 pages you'll read someday. It's the most useful furniture you own.

choices.label: Stand through lab meeting to make a point
choices.text: Nobody is sure what the point is. Then {labmate} stands too, and by spring lab meeting is twenty minutes shorter.

wellbeing.title: Sixth Floor
text: The elevator is out for a month. The sign says "We apologize for the inconvenience." The lab is on the sixth floor.

choices.label: Take the stairs, every time
choices.text: Six floors, four times a day. By week three you arrive only slightly out of breath.

choices.label: Work from the ground-floor library
choices.text: The library is quiet and warm. You get a lot done and miss all the lab gossip.

choices.label: Wait for the freight elevator
choices.text: It comes every twenty minutes. You get to know the custodians, and a lot of podcasts.

wellbeing.title: Daylight
text: You haven't seen daylight on a weekday in two weeks. You arrive and leave in the dark, and the lab has no windows.

success.text: {advisor} agrees to a walking meeting. It's cold and short, and the best meeting you've had this month.

failure.text: {advisor} agrees, and then it rains sideways. You take notes on a wet napkin.

choices.label: Trade desks with {labmate} for the window
choices.text: {labmate} agrees, for a week of coffee and a little sighing. The window faces a parking lot, but it's daylight.

choices.label: Buy a daylight lamp
choices.text: It is very bright and very blue. Your desk looks like a dentist's office, and you feel noticeably more awake.

wellbeing.title: The Stretch Timer
text: {labmate} sets up an hourly stretch timer for the whole lab. It goes off in the middle of your practice talk, right on the slide with the main result.

choices.label: Stretch with everyone
choices.text: The whole room stretches. You lose your place and never quite find it again, but everyone's shoulders thank you.

choices.label: Mute it
choices.text: You finish the talk on time. The timer stays muted for the rest of the month, for everyone.

choices.label: Lead the stretches from now on
choices.text: You become the lab's stretch captain. It costs five minutes an hour and earns you a lot of goodwill.

wellbeing.title: New Glasses
text: Your new glasses arrive. It turns out the slides at department talks were never blurry, and trees have individual leaves.

choices.label: Wear them everywhere
choices.text: After two days of headaches, the world gets sharper. You can now read the fine print on the reimbursement form, and you wish you couldn't.

choices.label: Keep them for screens only
choices.text: You still squint at the whiteboard, but your eyes stop aching by 6 pm.

choices.label: Reread your favorite paper, properly
choices.text: Figure 3 had error bars all along. The paper is even better than you remembered.

wellbeing.title: Day Two Without Coffee
text: You try quitting coffee for a week. Day two brings a headache with opinions and a personal grudge against the coffee machine.

choices.label: Push through to day seven
choices.text: A rough week, then a surprise: you sleep through the night and wake up before the alarm.

choices.label: Switch to tea
choices.text: You drink three cups of green tea a day and start describing it as "grassy".

choices.label: Give up at 10:02 am
choices.text: The coffee tastes like victory and defeat at the same time.

wellbeing.title: Regular Customer
text: The late-night delivery driver greets you by name. Last week they asked how the paper is going.

choices.label: Order the salad this time
choices.text: The driver looks worried about you. The salad is fine, and you're hungry again by midnight.

choices.label: Order the usual, extra fries
choices.text: The fries are perfect, and for ten minutes nothing else matters.

choices.label: Make it your last delivery this month
choices.text: You cook rice in bulk and eat it with whatever's in the fridge. The driver probably misses you.

wellbeing.title: Lunch Rotation
text: {labmate} starts a lab lunch rotation: each week, one person cooks for everyone. Your week is coming up.

choices.label: Cook something real
choices.text: A big pot of curry for nine people. It takes a whole day, and everyone has seconds.

choices.label: Bring store-bought dumplings
choices.text: Nobody minds. Two people ask where they're from. You let them believe it took effort.

choices.label: Keep eating at your desk
choices.text: You opt out and get a quiet hour every day. Through the door, you hear the lab laughing over lunch.

wellbeing.title: Leftovers in the Kitchen
text: The department's "leftovers in the kitchen" emails have fed you for a week, mostly pizza and one mysterious tray of wraps.

choices.label: Keep it up
choices.text: Your wallet is happy. You haven't eaten a vegetable since Tuesday.

choices.label: Buy actual groceries
choices.text: Vegetables! You'd forgotten how they crunch.

choices.label: Turn on notifications for the list
choices.text: You can now reach any kitchen in the building in 90 seconds, and you've met half the department over cold pizza.

wellbeing.title: The Checkup
text: Your student health plan includes a free checkup. The nurse asks how many hours a day you sit. You do the math out loud, which is a mistake.

choices.label: Answer honestly and take the advice
choices.text: Walk after lunch, stand up every hour, sleep seven hours. The first two turn out to be easy.

choices.label: Round down
choices.text: "About six," you say. The nurse writes down "twelve" and hands you a pamphlet anyway.

choices.label: Laugh nervously
choices.text: The nurse laughs too, then books you a follow-up that you will probably go to.

wellbeing.title: Fever on the Big Day
text: You wake up with a fever on the morning of your committee meeting. {committee} moved a flight to be there.

choices.label: Reschedule
choices.text: Everyone is kind about it. The next time all four of you are free is five weeks away. You spend two days in bed.

choices.label: Join by video from bed
choices.text: You present in a hoodie with a blanket on your shoulders. {committee} calls it the most relaxed meeting they've had all year.

choices.label: Go in person, sit far from everyone

success.text: You present from the far end of the table. It goes well, and nobody catches anything.

failure.text: Halfway through, you sneeze on the projector remote. {committee} is very gracious. You go straight to bed.

wellbeing.title: No Colds in the Clinic
text: You wake up with a cold the day before your {project} sessions with clinicians. Nobody brings a cold into a hospital.

choices.label: Reschedule the sessions
choices.text: The clinicians are understanding. Their next free slots are two weeks out. You spend the wait in bed with tea.

choices.label: Ask {labmate} to run them from your script

success.text: {labmate} follows your script to the letter and adds one great follow-up question. You owe them dinner.

failure.text: {labmate} is glad to help but skips the warm-up questions. The sessions happen; the data is thinner.

choices.label: Switch to video sessions
choices.text: Most of the clinicians prefer it anyway. You run them from your couch, muted between coughs.

wellbeing.title: No Voice
text: It's the morning you teach section, and your voice is gone. What comes out is a small, hopeful squeak.

choices.label: Teach from slides and the whiteboard
choices.text: You write everything down. It's the clearest section you've ever taught.

choices.label: Swap with another TA
choices.text: They cover for you and say you owe them one. They will collect, during finals.

choices.label: Whisper; the students lean in
choices.text: Thirty students lean in and go very quiet. It's the most attentive section all semester, and by evening your throat feels like sandpaper.

wellbeing.title: Soup at the Door
text: You're home with a cold. There's a knock, and outside your door is a container of soup and a sticky note from {labmate}: "Get well. Don't answer the lab chat."

choices.label: Rest properly, like the note says
choices.text: You eat the soup and sleep. By Friday you're back, and so is your sense of smell.

choices.label: Thank them, then work from bed
choices.text: You send a heart emoji and a pull request. The soup goes cold next to your laptop.

choices.label: Return the favor next week
choices.text: Once you're better, you bring {labmate} homemade dumplings. The lab now runs on a soup-and-dumplings economy.

wellbeing.title: Snow Day
text: Snow day: the university closes campus and locks the building. The whole city is quiet.

choices.label: Actually rest
choices.text: You read a novel with no citations under a blanket, which feels almost illegal.

choices.label: Write from home all day
choices.text: With no meetings and no seminar, you write more than you have all month.

choices.label: Have a snowball fight, then write
choices.text: {labmate} turns out to have a terrifying arm. Afterward, you write slowly over hot chocolate.

wellbeing.title: Black Ice
text: You slip on the ice outside the building and land on your hand. A sprained wrist: one-handed typing for a week.

choices.label: Rest it and dictate your writing
choices.text: Your laptop hears "in this paper" as "in this pepper" all week. Your wrist heals. Your draft is now well seasoned.

choices.label: Type one-handed, grimly
choices.text: Forty words a minute becomes nine. You discover how many of your sentences were optional.

choices.label: Pair-program with {labmate} at the keyboard
choices.text: You talk, they type. They fix two of your bugs out of pure impatience.

wellbeing.title: The Sneeze
text: You sneeze, hard, and something in your lower back says "no". You now walk like someone twice your age.

choices.label: Ice it and spend a day on the floor
choices.text: A whole day on the living-room floor with an ice pack and a podcast. There's a crack in the ceiling you'd never noticed.

choices.label: Work standing very still
choices.text: You stand at your desk like a heron for three days. It mostly works, until you drop a pen.

choices.label: Tell everyone it was a sports injury
choices.text: Nobody believes you. Everyone respects the commitment to the story.

wellbeing.title: Faculty vs. Students
text: It's the annual faculty-vs-students soccer match, and {advisor} is on the other team, wearing shin guards and the look they usually save for deadlines.

success.text: You score past {advisor}, who shakes your hand and brings it up at lab meeting for a month. You're sore all week.

failure.text: One big tackle and a pulled hamstring. The students win anyway, and you watch the second half with an ice pack.

choices.label: Go easy whenever your advisor has the ball
choices.text: {advisor} scores twice and is in a wonderful mood all week. Your teammates have noticed.

choices.label: Cheer from the sideline with snacks
choices.text: You bring orange slices and the loudest voice on the field. The students lose by one, but the snacks are a hit.

wellbeing.title: The Climbing Gym
text: {labmate} drags you to the climbing gym. You make it up two walls. The next morning, your forearms are too sore to hold a coffee, let alone type.

choices.label: Go again next week
choices.text: Week two: three walls, less shaking. {labmate} has a climbing buddy now.

choices.label: Stick to the easy wall
choices.text: The beginner wall is full of eight-year-olds who are better than you. It's good exercise anyway.

choices.label: Rest your hands and read papers instead
choices.text: You spend two days reading with your arms propped on pillows. Your forearms recover, and your reading list gets shorter.

wellbeing.title: Last Row
text: Fourteen hours on the plane to {city}: last row, next to the restroom, in a seat that reclines one inch, in theory.

choices.label: Walk the aisle every hour
choices.text: You do laps with a retired dentist and land with working legs.

choices.label: Put on an eye mask and sleep
choices.text: You sleep six of the fourteen hours, in eleven pieces.

choices.label: Finish your slides on the tray table
choices.text: The slides are done by landing. Your neck stays at tray-table angle for two days.

wellbeing.title: Wide Awake at 4 am
text: Jet lag wakes you at 4 am in {city}, wide awake and starving. The hotel gym opens at 5.

choices.label: Work out the minute it opens
choices.text: Forty minutes on a treadmill facing a mirror. By breakfast, your body has picked a time zone.

choices.label: Rehearse your talk in the empty lobby
choices.text: The night clerk hears your talk four times and has one very good question.

choices.label: Lie in the dark reading arXiv
choices.text: By sunrise you've read nine abstracts and remember none. You fall asleep at 7:50, ten minutes before your alarm.

wellbeing.title: 23,000 Steps
text: Your phone says you're walking 23,000 steps a day at {venue}. Your feet say more. Your conference shoes were chosen for looks.

choices.label: Buy comfortable shoes in {city}
choices.text: The ugliest, softest shoes in {city}. You miss a morning session finding them, then walk the rest of the week in bliss.

choices.label: Sit through the afternoon sessions
choices.text: Three hours in a dark room with your feet up on your bag. You learn a lot and meet nobody.

choices.label: Keep walking the poster hall
choices.text: Forty posters and twelve good conversations later, you have two blisters.

wellbeing.title: Forty Percent Croissant
text: Day three at {venue}. Since landing, you've eaten nothing but coffee-break pastries. You are now about 40% croissant.

choices.label: Find a grocery store
choices.text: You eat yogurt and a bag of carrots on a bench in {city}. You miss a session and don't regret it.

choices.label: Embrace it
choices.text: There's a cinnamon one today. Life is good, and slightly sticky.

choices.label: Save room for the reception
choices.text: You skip lunch to save room. The reception food is gone in four minutes. You eat a breadstick and talk to everyone.

choices.label: Find the bakery the locals line up for
choices.text: A tiny bakery with a line around the block. You bring a box back to your session and become very popular.

wellbeing.title: The Fun Run
text: The {venue} fun run starts at 6:30 am. Two authors whose papers you've cited many times have signed up.

success.text: You keep pace with them for five kilometers and talk the whole way. One of them asks for your paper.

failure.text: You last two kilometers, then walk. They wave as they pass. At the finish you say hi, very red in the face.

choices.label: Sleep in
choices.text: You sleep until 8 and see the finish-line photos at breakfast. Everyone looks happy and very sweaty.

choices.label: Walk it with a coffee, meet them at the end
choices.text: You arrive last, with coffee. They are delighted, mostly by the coffee, and you talk for twenty minutes.

wellbeing.title: Canceled
text: Your flight home from {city} is canceled overnight. The line for hotel vouchers is two hours long and not moving.

choices.label: Wait for the voucher
choices.text: Two hours later you have a voucher for a hotel by the highway. You sleep five hours and fly home grumpy.

choices.label: Sleep on the floor by the gate
choices.text: You build a bed out of a conference tote and your poster tube. You wake up first in line, with a crick in your neck.

choices.label: Work through the night on revisions
choices.text: At an empty gate at 3 am, you revise more than you have all month. You land looking like a ghost.

world.title: Everyone Pivots
text: {biglab} releases {model}. Within a week, every reading group and half of arXiv is about it.
{biglab} releases {model}, and the field changes its plans overnight. Three talks at this week's seminar are rewritten the morning of.

choices.label: Spend the weekend trying it
choices.text: You find two things it does brilliantly and one it gets hilariously wrong. You keep notes on all three.

success.text: While everyone chases {model}, you have your corner of the field to yourself.

failure.text: At lab meeting, three people ask why you're not using {model}. You don't have a great answer yet.

choices.label: Start a quick evaluation of it
choices.text: Your two-day evaluation finds where {model} breaks. People start emailing you about it.

world.title: Solved, Apparently
text: {biglab}'s announcement for {model} says it "solves" {project.topic}. You read the fine print. It was tested on forty easy examples.

choices.label: Test {model} on your data
choices.text: On your data, it gets 61%. Your paper now has a strong new baseline and a sharper story.

choices.label: Write a careful thread about it

success.text: Your thread is shared widely. Researchers send you their own failure cases.

failure.text: The thread gets four likes, two of them from labmates.

choices.label: Ignore it and keep working
choices.text: A month later nobody remembers the claim, except maybe your reviewers.

world.title: Suddenly Popular
text: Your topic, {project.topic}, is suddenly the hottest thing in the field: {roll:38-45} new papers this month alone.

choices.label: Rush to get yours out first
choices.text: You work three weekends straight. The draft moves fast, and a few corners get cut.

choices.label: Read every one of them
choices.text: Two overlap with yours. Now you know exactly what makes your work different.

success.text: Everyone is building systems, so you study the users instead.

failure.text: Every angle you find is already taken, sometimes twice.

world.title: Is It an Agent?
text: Suddenly every paper needs "agents", and the word is on every lab meeting slide. {labmate} asks whether {project} is an agent.

choices.label: Rebrand it as an agent
choices.text: Your slides say "agentic" eleven times. People seem more interested, and somewhat more confused.

choices.label: Explain that it's a pipeline
choices.text: "It's a pipeline." A few people nod. One of them is a reviewer, and they appreciate it.

choices.label: Build a real agent version
choices.text: You spend a week on it. It works, and it's more interesting than the buzzword.

world.title: Does It Mean Anything?
text: A field-wide online debate breaks out: does the benchmark behind {project} measure anything at all? The top post has {roll:900-3000} replies.

choices.label: Add a second evaluation
choices.text: A small human evaluation backs up your numbers. It costs a week and makes the paper much harder to attack.

choices.label: Join the debate
choices.text: You post a careful take and spend two days answering replies. Some of them are useful.

choices.label: Write an honest limitations paragraph
choices.text: You write one clear paragraph on what the benchmark can and can't tell you. Reviewers tend to like that.

world.title: A Famous Post
text: A famous researcher posts about {paper}: "This is the kind of work the field needs." Your phone does not stop buzzing for an hour.

choices.label: Reply with a short thank-you
choices.text: You keep it short and gracious. A few hundred people read your paper this week.

choices.label: Post a thread explaining the paper

success.text: The thread takes off. Three labs email you about follow-up work.

failure.text: The replies turn into an argument about your figure's font. Some people read the paper anyway.

choices.label: Send a screenshot to your parents
choices.text: Your parents don't fully get it, but they print it out and put it on the fridge.

world.title: Pioneering Work
text: A new survey paper calls {paper} "pioneering work". You read the sentence three times to make sure it's yours.

choices.label: Email the authors a thank-you
choices.text: They reply warmly and ask whether you'd review their next draft.

choices.label: Add it to your research statement
choices.text: "Described as pioneering by a recent survey." It reads well in the statement.

choices.label: Read how they describe it
choices.text: They get it mostly right, which is more than most citations do.

world.title: The Freeze
text: Three companies on your list announce hiring freezes in the same week. One recruiter writes to "keep in touch for next year".

choices.label: Widen your search
choices.text: You add twelve more places and a few you'd never considered. It's a long weekend of cover letters.

choices.label: Ask {advisor} about a postdoc
choices.text: Your advisor has a few ideas and a few names. Suddenly the year ahead looks less frozen.

success.text: A former labmate's team still has one open position. They forward your CV that afternoon.

failure.text: Everyone you ask is frozen too. A few promise to let you know when things thaw.

world.title: Offers, Unasked
text: Hiring is booming. Two recruiters you've never met email you about summer internships, and one even spells your name right.

choices.label: Take both calls
choices.text: Both recruiters are friendly, and both calls end with a next step.

choices.label: Ask {advisor} which one fits
choices.text: Your advisor knows someone on one of the teams. Your reply now sounds much better informed.

choices.label: Archive them, you're busy
choices.text: Your research gets the week. In this market, the recruiters will write again.

world.title: Back in Fashion
text: A method from the 2010s is suddenly back in fashion. Half of today's new papers cite something older than your undergrad degree.

choices.label: Read the original paper
choices.text: It's surprisingly good, and it has a section everyone forgot about.

choices.label: Ask {senior} what it was like
choices.text: {senior} talks for an hour. You learn more than the papers taught you.

choices.label: Post "we had this in 2014"
choices.text: It gets a lot of likes from people who were there, and a lot of replies from people who weren't.

world.title: The Daily Listing
text: Today's arXiv listing in your area is {roll:380-460} papers long.
You open today's arXiv listing. It is {roll:380-460} papers long, and it's only Tuesday.

choices.label: Skim every title
choices.text: An hour later, you have seven open tabs and a mild headache.

success.text: Nothing overlaps with your work, and you relax a little.

failure.text: One paper looks close. After an hour of reading, you decide it probably isn't.

choices.label: Close the tab
choices.text: If a paper matters, someone in the lab chat will post it.

world.title: Is This Still Relevant?
text: Your topic, {project.topic}, has gone quiet. After your seminar talk on {project}, someone asks, kindly: "Is this still relevant?"

success.text: You connect it to the question everyone is asking now. Suddenly it's the angle nobody else has.

failure.text: The new framing confuses everyone, including your own abstract.

choices.label: Show who still needs it
choices.text: You find three real deployments with exactly this problem. Your introduction gets a new first paragraph.

choices.label: Keep going: less hype, less competition
choices.text: With fewer people to race, you make steady progress. A few doubts creep in at night.

world.title: Twice the Papers
text: The flagship conference got {roll:18000-24000} submissions this cycle, double last year. The reviewer pool did not double. An email asks if you can take "a few" extra reviews.

choices.label: Volunteer for six extra reviews
choices.text: You review six papers in a week. Now you know what everyone else is working on, and you're tired.

choices.label: Make {project} readable in five minutes
choices.text: You rewrite the abstract, Figure 1 and every first sentence for a reviewer who only skims.

choices.label: Decline. It's a lottery anyway
choices.text: You turn down the extra reviews and keep your week. The deadline still feels like a lottery.

world.title: A Brand-New Venue
text: A new conference launches. It has no track record yet, but it has a very nice logo. {advisor} calls submitting there "a gamble, but a fun one".

choices.label: Volunteer to review for it
choices.text: You review four papers for the first edition. The organizers remember who showed up early.

choices.label: Put its deadline in your calendar
choices.text: It goes next to the big ones, in a slightly smaller font. You read the call twice and like it.

choices.label: Wait and see if it lasts
choices.text: Most new venues fade. You'll keep an eye on it from a safe distance.

world.title: The Gamble Paid Off
text: The brand-new conference from two years ago is now where everyone wants to publish. Its acceptance rate is 19%, and people call it "basically top-tier" in hushed voices.

choices.label: Mention you were there at the start
choices.text: The first-edition crowd has a group chat now. You're in it, and so are two of this year's program chairs.

choices.label: Read its best papers
choices.text: The bar is high and the papers are good. Its deadline goes in your calendar, in full-size font.

choices.label: Remember everyone calling it a gamble
choices.text: You keep that memory to yourself, mostly. Prestige, it turns out, takes about two years.

world.title: The New Checklist
text: Your target venues adopt a new reproducibility checklist: random seeds, compute hours, code links and the exact prompts you used. For {project}, you can answer about half.

choices.label: Answer honestly, gaps and all
choices.text: Half the answers say "not recorded". It stings, but reviewers tend to respect that.
choices.tip: Hold Yourself to a High Standard

choices.label: Rerun things until every answer is yes
choices.text: After a week of reruns with every seed logged, every box is a confident yes. You feel slightly less confident in general.

choices.label: Write a logging script for the future

success.text: Your script records every seed and GPU hour automatically. Half the lab asks for a copy.

failure.text: The script logs everything, including 40 GB of things nobody needs.

writing.title: The Bug After the Deadline
text: Three days after submitting {paper}, you find a bug in your evaluation script: it counted some test examples twice. Fixed, your gain over the best baseline drops from 4.1 points to 1.9.
Rerunning one table for fun, you find a bug in your analysis script. The corrected numbers still support {paper}, but the headline gain is half of what the submission says.

choices.label: Email the program chairs tonight
choices.text: The chairs thank you and pass the correction to the reviewers. Your advisor replies: "This is exactly right. Thank you." It stings less than you expected.
choices.tip: Hold Yourself to a High Standard

choices.label: Disclose it in the author response

success.text: You open the response with the correction and the new numbers. Reviewer 1 thanks you for the transparency, and the smaller gain still holds.

failure.text: The correction ends up in paragraph four. Reviewer 2 finds it there and now doubts every number in the paper.

choices.label: Fix it in the camera-ready, tell nobody
choices.text: You add "update Table 2" to your to-do list and tell nobody. It sits there like a pebble in your shoe.

choices.label: "It's only two points." Let it go
choices.text: You close the script. The paper is under review, and the numbers are what they are. Something about that sentence keeps bothering you.

writing.title: Spot the Difference
text: A careful reader emails you. The numbers in Table 2 of your latest version differ from the ones reviewers saw, and nothing in the paper says why.

choices.label: Add a correction note today
choices.text: Two sentences and a footnote explain the fix. It costs you a little pride and earns you some respect.

choices.label: Reply privately and explain
choices.text: They accept your explanation and thank you. You wonder how many readers noticed and didn't write.

choices.label: Leave the email unanswered
choices.text: Their second email copies your advisor. Your advisor's note to you afterwards is very short.

writing.title: The Polite Email
text: A student at another university ran your released code and got numbers two points below your paper. Their email is very polite, and they attached their logs.

choices.label: Thank them and post a correction
choices.text: The correction goes up, late, with their name in it. They cite you anyway.
choices.tip: Hold Yourself to a High Standard

choices.label: Tell your advisor first
choices.text: Your advisor is quiet for a moment, then helps you write the correction. "Next time, tell me the day you find it."

choices.label: Blame the random seeds
choices.text: They run ten seeds and send you a plot. Their paper cites yours, in a footnote about reproducibility.

writing.title: Christmas in the Lab
text: Winter break. The building is empty, and for once so is the GPU queue. {project} still needs two experiments and half a rewrite.
Your family asks when you're coming home for the holidays. You look at {project}, then at the empty GPU queue, then back at the message.

choices.label: Spend the whole break on it
choices.text: You run experiments by day and rewrite by night, with family calls on mute. By New Year the paper is much better, and you are much more tired.

choices.label: Work mornings, family evenings
choices.text: The experiments run while you eat dinner. Progress is slower, but you will remember that the holidays happened.

choices.label: Take the whole break off
choices.text: You leave the laptop closed for two weeks and eat too much. You come back rested, with the same paper and a clearer idea of what it needs.

choices.label: Run jobs while everyone sleeps
choices.text: Jobs launch at 1 am and finish by breakfast. Your family thinks you're on vacation. The cluster knows better.

writing.title: Twelve Into Eight
text: The draft of {project} is 12 pages. {venue} allows 8. The deadline is tomorrow night.
You compile the final draft and scroll to the end: page 12. The limit is 8.

success.text: Eight pages, and somehow clearer than twelve. Half the cuts were sentences that said the same thing twice.

failure.text: It fits in eight pages, but Section 4 lost the sentences that explained it. Now nobody, including you, can follow it.

choices.label: Move everything to the appendix
choices.text: The main paper fits. Reviewers don't have to read the appendix, and they won't.

choices.label: Shrink the fonts and the spacing
choices.text: It fits. Table 2 is now in 7-point type, and Figure 3 needs a magnifying glass.

choices.label: Rewrite it in half the words
choices.text: You cut every paragraph in half, and it reads better than the long version ever did.

writing.title: Overleaf Is Down
text: Two hours before the {venue} deadline, Overleaf stops loading. The status page says "investigating". So does everyone in your lab chat.
You click Recompile and nothing happens, so you refresh. Overleaf is down, and the {venue} deadline is in two hours.

choices.label: Compile locally from your last sync

success.text: Your last sync was 20 minutes ago. You finish in a local editor and submit with time to spare.

failure.text: Your local copy is from last Tuesday. You redo a week of edits from memory and submit at 11:58 pm.

choices.label: Wait and keep refreshing
choices.text: It comes back after 50 minutes. You spend the last hour fixing only what matters, which turns out to be a skill.

choices.label: Submit this morning's PDF
choices.text: Submitted at 10:02 pm, minus tonight's fixes. You go to bed while everyone else refreshes.

choices.label: Build it from your own git mirror
choices.text: The mirror you set up two years ago, for exactly this night, is five minutes behind. You submit calmly.

writing.title: 11:45 pm
text: At 11:45 pm, {labmate} pushes a big change to {project}: a rewritten Section 4 and a new results table. The deadline is midnight.
Fifteen minutes before the deadline, the edit history lights up. {labmate} is rewriting your related work, live.

success.text: It compiles, and the new version is honestly better than yours.

failure.text: It compiles with 14 undefined references. Every cell of the new table reads "??".

choices.label: Revert to your version
choices.text: You submit your version at 11:57. {labmate} says "no worries" in a tone that suggests worries.

choices.label: Merge only what you can check
choices.text: You read each change once and keep about half. You submit at 11:59:40, heart racing.

writing.title: 48 More Hours
text: At 9 pm, the chairs extend the {venue} deadline by 48 hours. {project} was nearly done, and now it doesn't have to be.

choices.label: Use all 48 hours
choices.text: You use all 48 hours. The paper gets better and you get worse.

choices.label: Polish for one day, then sleep
choices.text: After a day of fixes and a full night's sleep, you submit with 20 hours to spare. Nobody in your lab believes you.

choices.label: Submit now and go to bed
choices.text: You submit at 9:15 pm and sleep for eleven hours. Everyone else uses all 48.

choices.label: Start the real work at hour 40
choices.text: Forty hours of feeling that you have time, then eight hours of doing more than you did all month.

writing.title: Comments, Six Hours Out
text: Six hours before the deadline, {advisor}'s comments on {project} arrive: {roll:30-60} of them, three starting with "Big question:".

choices.label: Address every comment
choices.text: You get through all of them with ten minutes to spare. The big questions were the right questions.

success.text: You fix the three that matter and leave the commas for the camera-ready. Your advisor agrees with your triage.

failure.text: You fix three comments carefully. Comment 17, which you skipped, was the important one.

choices.label: "Will fix in the camera-ready!"
choices.text: You submit as is. Your advisor replies "ok." Just "ok."

writing.title: What If the Title Were a Question?
text: An hour before the deadline, {advisor} sends a message: "What if the title were a question?"
Fifty minutes to go. {advisor} writes: "New title idea. Hear me out." It has a colon and a pun.

choices.label: Take it and fix every mention
choices.text: The new title is catchier. You change it in six places, then find a seventh.

success.text: "Fair. It's your paper." You keep your title, and your advisor seems to respect you a little more for asking.

failure.text: "Ok." The period does a lot of work.

choices.label: Promise to revisit it later
choices.text: You agree to change it for the camera-ready. You both know nobody changes the title for the camera-ready.

writing.title: Service Unavailable
text: At 11:58 pm you click Submit. The {venue} submission system shows a spinning wheel, then "503 Service Unavailable".

success.text: It goes through at 12:00:41 and counts anyway, because the server's clock was down too.

failure.text: It goes through at 12:03, with final_v2.pdf instead of final_v3.pdf. Your hands were shaking.

choices.label: Email your PDF to the chairs
choices.text: A form reply at 12:20 am: everything submitted during the outage will be accepted. Hundreds of people got the same reply.

choices.label: Post the error screenshot online
choices.text: Two thousand people post the same screenshot. The chairs add an hour, and you spend most of it reading the replies.

writing.title: Limitations, 3 am
text: It's 3 am. {venue} requires a Limitations section, and yours is a heading with nothing under it.

success.text: You list them plainly: small sample, one language, one site. The paper is more convincing for it.

failure.text: It's honest and slightly unhinged. One sentence starts with "Frankly,", which you'll fix in the camera-ready.

choices.label: Paste the generic version
choices.text: "Our method may not generalize to all settings." Reviewers have read that sentence four hundred times.

choices.label: Turn each limitation into future work
choices.text: Every weakness is now an "exciting direction". Reviewers have seen that trick before, too.

choices.label: Sleep four hours, write it at 7 am

success.text: After four hours of sleep, the section takes 40 minutes, and it's the clearest page in the paper.

failure.text: You sleep through two alarms and write the whole section in 12 minutes, mostly as bullet points.

writing.title: Name Already Taken
text: An hour before submitting {project}, you finally search your method's acronym. Four papers already use it, and so does a robot vacuum.

success.text: Twenty minutes of backronyms later, you have a name nobody has used. It almost spells a word.

failure.text: The best you can manage has a hyphen and the number 2 in it. It is unique, at least.

choices.label: Keep it and hope nobody checks
choices.text: Somebody will check. A reviewer will write: "Not to be confused with the four other methods of the same name."

choices.label: Drop it and say "our method"
choices.text: Without the acronym, the paper reads a little plainer and a little clearer.

writing.title: Anonymous, Mostly
text: Rereading the submitted PDF, you click the code link. It opens your personal GitHub page, with your photo and a README thanking your advisor.
An hour after submitting {paper}, you realize the footnote with the code link was never anonymized. It points straight to your GitHub account.

choices.label: Take the repo down tonight
choices.text: The link now leads to a 404. One reviewer will write "code not available", which is fair.

choices.label: Scrub the repo and rename the account

success.text: You rename the account and wipe its history, down to a README that thanks nobody. The link now belongs to a stranger.

failure.text: A search engine had already cached the old page, and the program chairs find it before any reviewer does. Desk rejected.

success.text: The chairs reply within a day: send an anonymous link, and they'll pass it on to the reviewers.

failure.text: The chairs thank you for flagging it, then apply the policy. Desk rejected, very politely.

writing.title: Wrong Track
text: The confirmation email arrives, and you read the track name twice. You picked the one just above the one you meant.
Rereading the confirmation, you notice that {paper} went to the theory track. It contains no theorems.

choices.label: Email the chairs to move it

success.text: Moved within a day, with a smiley face. The chairs see this every cycle.

failure.text: Reviewers were already assigned, and the chairs are sorry. The reviewers will be sorry too.

choices.label: Leave it there for fresh eyes

success.text: The out-of-area reviewers find the paper refreshing. One calls it "a welcome change of pace".

failure.text: Reviewer 1 writes: "This does not belong in this track." Reviewer 1 is correct.

writing.title: Is That How You Spell It?
text: The camera-ready is in. Then {labmate}, your co-author, messages: "Small thing. My name is spelled wrong." It is, in the proceedings metadata.

success.text: Fixed within a day. The chairs say they get this email a lot, which helps a little.

failure.text: The PDF gets fixed, but the metadata doesn't. Search engines will remember both spellings forever.

choices.label: Apologize over lunch, then email
choices.text: The chairs fix it eventually. The lunch, slightly awkward, fixes the friendship right away.

choices.label: Fix the preprint and move on
choices.text: The preprint is right, and the official version is wrong forever. {labmate} says it's fine, twice.

writing.title: Langauge
text: The camera-ready is submitted. You open the PDF to admire it, and the first sentence of the abstract says "langauge".
Final version, uploaded. You flip through it once more and find "Tabel 3" on page 6, in a sentence you've read forty times.

success.text: The chair lets you upload a fixed PDF, with a gentle note that the window closes tomorrow.

failure.text: The proceedings are final. The typo is now part of the permanent scientific record.

choices.label: Fix the preprint and let it go
choices.text: The preprint is perfect. The official version has character.

choices.label: Fix it, and every orphan word too

success.text: One typo and 23 orphan words later, not a single paragraph ends on a lonely word. You print page 1 just to look at it.

failure.text: You fix 31 orphan words. Each fix creates a new one somewhere else. At 2 am, you stop.

writing.title: Figure 1, Day 3
text: Figure 1 for {project} is on its third day. It has been a pipeline diagram, a comic strip, and a pipeline diagram again.
You've spent three days on Figure 1. It's two boxes and an arrow, and it's still not right.

choices.label: Give it one more day
choices.text: On day four it clicks: one picture that explains the whole paper. Reviewers will look at it before they read a word.

choices.label: Ship the version from day one
choices.text: Nobody has ever rejected a paper over a fine Figure 1, probably.

success.text: {labmate} moves one arrow and deletes two boxes, and suddenly the figure makes sense.

failure.text: {labmate} suggests making it 3D. You thank them and lose another afternoon talking them out of it.

writing.title: Introduction, Version 7
text: You open intro_v7.tex, then, out of curiosity, intro_v1.tex. Version one was better.
The seventh rewrite of the introduction to {project} is done. You reread the first one, and it was better.

choices.label: Go back to version one
choices.text: Seven drafts to learn that the first one was right. At least now you know why it's right.

choices.label: Merge the best of all seven

success.text: Version one's argument, version five's opening line, version seven's citations. It's the best one yet.

failure.text: Version eight reads like seven people wrote it, which, in a way, they did.

choices.label: Start version eight
choices.text: Version eight is slightly better than version one. It took another week.

writing.title: Abstract Due First
text: Surprise: the abstract for {project} is due a week before the paper. The experiments aren't finished, so neither is the story.
The submission site wants a title and abstract for {project} by Friday, a week before the full paper. You have a title.

choices.label: Submit a placeholder abstract
choices.text: "We study an important problem and find interesting results." Everyone does this, and you can rewrite it on deadline night.

choices.label: Write the real abstract now
choices.text: Two hundred words take a whole day and force you to say what's actually new. Now you know what the paper is about.

choices.label: Write the abstract you hope is true

success.text: The results come in and match it almost word for word. You decide you planned it that way.

failure.text: The results come in and disagree with paragraph two. You rewrite the abstract, then the paper around it.

writing.title: Related Work, Page Two
text: The related work section of {project} is now two pages long. It cites {roll:80-110} papers, including one you've only read the title of.
You meant to write one paragraph of related work for {project}. It's two pages now, with subsections.

choices.label: Cut it to half a page

success.text: You sort it into three themes, one paragraph each, and end on what nobody has done yet. Now the gap is obvious.

failure.text: Half a page, and you cut the one paper most likely to be your reviewer's.

choices.label: Keep all two pages
choices.text: Every reviewer will find their own paper in there. The method now starts on page five.

choices.label: Turn it into a comparison table
choices.text: The table takes a day. Of thirteen rows, yours is the only one with every checkmark.

writing.title: Anywhere on Earth
text: At 11:40 pm, {labmate} reminds you that the {venue} deadline is Anywhere on Earth, which you had converted wrong. You have four more hours than you thought.

choices.label: Use all four hours
choices.text: You fix a table and sharpen the introduction. Then you watch a 4 am sunrise you didn't ask for.

choices.label: Submit now and go to bed
choices.text: You submit at 11:45 pm, as planned, and sleep while the rest of your lab finds new typos.

choices.label: Fix Figure 1, then stop
choices.text: You spend one hour on the figure everyone looks at first, then submit while you're ahead.

writing.title: Question 14
text: Question 14 of the {venue} responsible-research checklist: "Did you report the total compute used, in GPU hours?" You did not. You have no idea.
The {venue} checklist asks how many hours of annotation went into your data. You did most of it yourself, at night, without a stopwatch.

choices.label: Dig through the logs and find out

success.text: An hour of digging gives you a real number and a new appendix table. Reviewers love a real number.

failure.text: Half the logs were deleted to save disk space. You report an estimate, with a footnote that apologizes.

choices.label: Answer "No" and explain why
choices.text: "No, but here is roughly what it would be." It costs one paragraph, and nobody can say you hid anything.

choices.label: Answer "N/A"
choices.text: It is applicable. You both know it is applicable. You click Submit anyway.

writing.title: New Template, New Errors
text: This year's conference template is out. You paste in the draft of {project}, and nothing compiles: {roll:40-90} errors, all about a package you've never heard of.

success.text: Two hours and one deleted package later, it compiles. You post the fix in the lab chat and are briefly famous.

failure.text: It compiles by evening. Every table is now in a slightly different font, and you can't unsee it.

choices.label: Ask {senior}, who fixed it last year

success.text: {senior} replies in two minutes with a one-line fix and a sigh you can hear through the chat.

failure.text: {senior} is away, and the auto-reply points to the lab wiki. The wiki page was last edited four templates ago.

choices.label: Stay on last year's template for now
choices.text: Everything compiles today. The switch will happen later, at the least convenient moment possible.
